TERMS OF REFERENCE

INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT FOR AFRICA MONITORING, EVALUATION AND REPORTING TOOL (AMERT) SYSTEM SUPPORT

 

REF: ET-AUC-564012-CS-INDV

I. Background

 

The African Union Commission (AUC) has developed the Africa Monitoring, Evaluation and Reporting Tool (AMERT) as a comprehensive web-based platform to support Results-Based Management (RBM) across African Union programmes and operations. The system facilitates planning, implementation monitoring, performance tracking, evaluation of outputs and outcomes, and generation of reports aligned with Agenda 2063, the AU Strategic Plan, and other institutional reporting frameworks.

 

As AMERT continues to expand across AUC Departments, AU Organs and Specialized Agencies, there is an increasing demand for dedicated technical support to ensure optimum system performance, timely user assistance, continuous user capacity development, and sustained system adoption across the African Union.

 

The engagement of an IT Consultant will strengthen AMERT technical support services, improve user experience, facilitate continuous training, and contribute to effective implementation of Results-Based Management within the African Union.

 

II. Objective of the Assignment

 

To provide administrative and technical support to the AMERT Project Team by ensuring efficient operation of the AMERT platform, providing quality user support services, developing user documentation, conducting user training, and promoting effective utilization of the system across the African Union. The Consultant shall serve as one of the primary focal points for AMERT users and contribute to continuous system improvement through user engagement and technical support.

 

III. Scope of Work

 

The Consultant shall undertake, but not be limited to, the following responsibilities:

  1. Provide first-line technical support to AMERT users by responding to user queries received through email and other approved AU communication channels in a timely and professional manner.

Post Title: Jubbaland State Liaison Officer

Background

Jubbaland State Liaison Officer is required by the Federal Government of Somalia (FGS) to support implementation of a World Bank-funded project, Building Opportunities and Outcomes in Social Protection and Youth Employment (BOOST You) (P507443). The selected candidate will work for the government’s National Social Protection Program (Baxnaano), established in 2019 and housed at the Federal Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs (MoLSA).

Project Overview

The project development objective of Building Opportunities and Outcomes in Social Protection and Youth Employment (BOOST-YOU) is to enhance economic opportunities and strengthen resilience of the poor and vulnerable. The project directly contributes to strengthening Somalia’s social protection system, expanding coverage through its support to the jobs agenda and building greater resilience to shocks through robust adaptive social protection mechanisms. The project applies an integrated approach that moves beneficiaries along a continuum from protection to production.

The project aims to support the poor and most vulnerable of the population by providing targeted interventions to improve their resilience and prepare for better jobs tomorrow, while providing job opportunities now by addressing key barriers to better income-generating opportunities. The project will reach about 206,000 households in particularly climate-exposed areas, which is equivalent to over 1.2 million individual beneficiaries.

SELECTION CRITERIA

Selection shall be based on the qualification and experience of the candidate and followed by an interview. The qualifications, experience and skills should include:

Academic Qualifications

  1. Bachelor’s degree in one of the following areas: development studies, social work, management, public administration or business administration or any other relevant fields;

Professional Experience

  1. Five (5) years of relevant working experience at the national or international level in project/program coordination and management areas including humanitarian organizations, international NGOs, and government.
  2. Demonstrated knowledge of the Somalia development agenda, mechanisms and principles of social protection, Safety net programs and intra-governmental processes;
  3. Proven skills and ability in effectively communicating with and coordinating across diverse groups of stakeholders, including project staff, partners, government authorities, private sector, communities as well as beneficiaries;
  4. Demonstrated experience in stakeholder engagement, community mobilization, or participatory development approaches.
  5. Excellent communication (spoken and written) skills in Somali and English, including the ability to communicate proactively with key stakeholders, correctly interpret messages from others and respond appropriately.

                                   State Liaison Officer (Jubbaland)

                               Youth Employment (P507443) Project

Background

Jubbaland State Liaison Officer is required by the Federal Government of Somalia (FGS) to support implementation of a World Bank-funded project, Building Opportunities and Outcomes in Social Protection and Youth Employment (BOOST You) (P507443). The selected candidate will work for the government’s National Social Protection Program (Baxnaano), established in 2019 and housed at the Federal Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs (MoLSA).

Project Overview

The project development objective of Building Opportunities and Outcomes in Social Protection and Youth Employment (BOOST-YOU) is to enhance economic opportunities and strengthen resilience of the poor and vulnerable. The project directly contributes to strengthening Somalia’s social protection system, expanding coverage through its support to the jobs agenda and building greater resilience to shocks through robust adaptive social protection mechanisms. The project applies an integrated approach that moves beneficiaries along a continuum from protection to production.

The project aims to support the poor and most vulnerable of the population by providing targeted interventions to improve their resilience and prepare for better jobs tomorrow, while providing job opportunities now by addressing key barriers to better income-generating opportunities. The project will reach about 206,000 households in particularly climate-exposed areas, which is equivalent to over 1.2 million individual beneficiaries.

The program supports poor and vulnerable households through following components:

Component 1: Connecting Youth and Women to Better Jobs Today: Supports 28,000 youth (60% women & 5% disable persons) in urban areas with limited job opportunities and prolonged periods of inactivity, benefit from economic inclusion activities (wage and self-employment activities). contributing directly creating jobs and strengthening households’ resilience.

Component 2: Investing in People for Better Jobs Tomorrow: The component will deliver regular cash transfers to 50,000 of the poorest households to meet basic needs, enhance climate-challenged food security, and prevent negative coping strategies during climate shocks, which in turn helps safeguard the human capital necessary for productive participation in the labor force. Approximately 10,000 shock affected poor and vulnerable households will be supported with emergency cash transfers as part of a contingent financing arrangement in case of climate shocks. 30,000 pregnant women and mothers with children under two will receive health- and nutrition-linked co-responsibility cash transfers (CCTs) to promote maternal and child health, reduce malnutrition, and improve early childhood development, strengthening the human capital necessary for future workforce productivity whilst mitigating adverse climate impacts. An early response-Health and Nutrition CCT will support 83,000 shock affected households with pregnant women and mothers with children under two to reduce the prevalence of significant acute malnutrition and infant mortality in drought affected prioritized districts. An education CCT program will target 5,000 children from the poorest and most climate-affected households, helping build the foundation required for long-term employability by increasing school enrollment and attendance.

Component 3: Adaptive Social Protection Systems and Project Management: Supports enhancement of an adaptive social protection system, the National Socio-Economic Survey and project management including institutional capacity building for MoLSA. The objective of this support is to create a robust, efficient, and responsive social protection infrastructure. By strengthening institutional capacity, enhancing data management, strengthening the delivery system and registering the population in the USR, this component lays the foundation for sustainable and effective social protection and multisectoral poverty targeted investments. Under this component National Socio-economic Survey (NSES) will register 12 million people in Somalia in the USR collecting socio-economic data to inform targeting for pro-poor programs in the country. The component also provides support for effective project management, capacity building and oversight of project activities.

OBJECTIVE AND SCOPE OF WORK:

The State Liaison Officer will report to the Operations Team Lead and will be responsible for the implementation and delivery of all activities supported under the project. The State Liaison Officer must ensure compliance with operational protocols in the Baxnaano Operations Manual and accompanying guidelines, ensuring close coordination with relevant ministries, authorities, agencies and departments on day-to-day operational issues.

The Liaison Officer will help to coordinate the implementation of project activities at the State level between the PIU of the MoLSA, WFP and the relevant representatives of the Federal Member State (FMS), as well as other consultants (individuals and firms), hired under the project to facilitate effective delivery of project activities to achieve the overall project objectives. The Liaison Officer will work closely with the MOLSA PIU team and other implementing partners.

 

Under the leadership of the Operations Team Lead, duties of the State Liaison Officer will include:

 

  • Serve as a primary point of contact and sensitize the relevant representatives at counterpart ministries at the FMS level, community-based organizations (CBOs) and other social partners on social protection to create support for the project at the FMS level
  • Facilitate cooperation between the MoLSA/FGS and the relevant representatives at counterpart ministries at the FMS level on project activities and communicate priorities and concerns of the represented State to the PIU at the FGS level;
  • Coordinate with the relevant representatives at counterpart ministries at the State, the PIU/MoLSA, and field teams of WFP, as well as the CBOs and other social protection partners to support the implementation of the project in his/her state;
  • Attend and organize relevant meetings to support the implementation and coordination of Baxnaano activities, as requested by the representing State and the PIU/MoLSA
  • Prepare briefing notes, debriefs, reports necessary for the implementation and coordination of Baxnaano activities etc. and ensure follow-up on the represented State progress, as required;
  • Notify the PIU/MoLSA of pending and important issues to be raised during social protection meetings
  • Represent PIU at meetings, conferences and other relevant events at FMS level. Present PIUs position and safeguard its interest while coordinating with different stakeholders, in a professional manner. Share feedback and reports with PIU after attending the meetings/ events.
  • Recommend responses and action plans as a result of interacting with the project’s field team and the local community
  • Enable the flow of information between all relevant parties, particularly the relevant representatives at counterpart ministries at the represented State, including on potential risks and reporting immediately to the PIU/MoLSA complaints related to the Baxnaano in line with BOOST YOU complaints procedure for the PIU/MoLSA to respond as necessary;
  • Act as the State-level focal point for the project Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM), ensuring timely, transparent, and accountable handling of complaints Maintain proper documentation and reporting of grievances, ensuring confidentiality and data protection.
  • Support implementation and operationalization of the GRM in line with project procedures, including intake, registration, tracking, resolution, and feedback to complainants.
  • Maintain strict confidentiality of SEA/SH cases and ensure information is shared only on a need-to-know basis in accordance with established protocols.
  • Facilitate immediate referral of SEA/SH survivors to appropriate service providers (health, psychosocial, legal) in line with the project’s referral pathway.
  • Immediately escalate high-risk complaints (including SEA/SH, fraud, or serious social conflict) to PIU following established protocols.
  • Assist PIU in organizing and coordinating USR survey related meetings, workshops and training sessions at FMS level.
  • Ensure affective planning in consultation with PIU and WFP teams to ensure execution of smooth USR survey activities in the FMS. Affectively coordinate with concerned FMS ministries and district administration to streamline the field activities of USR survey.
  • Coordinate deployment of survey teams in the field with concerned stakeholders including facilitation in provision of any approvals, field security and help in arrangement of logistics.
  • Collaborate with third party monitoring firms (hired by MoLSA)
  • Assist the Operations Team Lead in preparing periodic reports on the field activities and progress of surveys.
  • Assist in improving communication and information sharing between different stakeholders.
  • Liaise and coordinate with third party monitoring teams and ensure that all activities are carried out as per program design.
  • Oversee the activities of third party Beneficiary Communication and Outreach firm in liaison with PIU to ensure that the campaign is conducted as per the agreed SOPs.
  • Facilitate third party firms to complete their activities avoiding potential bottlenecks. Suggest improvements to PIU, based on lessons learned in the field.
  • In collaboration with relevant representatives at counterpart ministries at the represented State, the PIU/MoLSA, and field teams of WFP, organize and participate in community sensitization and outreach activities to raise awareness to develop greater understanding of BOOST YOU and enhanced community partnership/commitment for the Baxnaano program;
  • Ensure that community engagement processes are culturally appropriate, accessible, gender-sensitive, and conflict-sensitive.
  • Facilitate regular community consultations, focus group discussions, and outreach sessions to enhance transparency and accountability of project interventions.
  • Monitor and report on stakeholder engagement activities, including participation levels, key concerns raised, and responses provided.
  • Compile and share reports about particular incidents, events, or updates on important issue for the project
  • Participate in trainings, workshops, supervision and implementation support missions conducted by the World Bank, and ‘learning-by-doing’ opportunities related to the BOOST YOU, as requested by the PIU;
  • Perform any other duties as required by PIU/ Operations Team Lead or Project Manager and/or represented FMS authority.

STATEMENT OF QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE:

The candidates should have the following desired qualifications:

  1. Bachelor’s degree in one of the following areas: development studies, social work, management, public administration or business administration or any other relevant fields;
  2. Five (5) years of relevant working experience at the national or international level in project/program coordination and management areas including humanitarian organizations, international NGOs, and government.
  3. Demonstrated knowledge of the Somalia development agenda, mechanisms and principles of social protection, Safety net programs and intra-governmental processes;
  4. Proven skills and ability in effectively communicating with and coordinating across diverse groups of stakeholders, including project staff, partners, government authorities, private sector, communities as well as beneficiaries;
  5. Demonstrated experience in stakeholder engagement, community mobilization, or participatory development approaches.
  6. Excellent communication (spoken and written) skills in Somali and English, including the ability to communicate proactively with key stakeholders, correctly interpret messages from others and respond appropriately. The candidate will demonstrate openness in sharing information;

CONDUCT OF WORK:

Reporting: The State Liaison Officer will directly report on a day-to-day basis to the Project Manager, Baxnaano through the Operations Team Lead. He/she will be expected to closely work with other Baxnaano PIU members for a smooth run of project operations. 

Language: Reports and other documents shall be submitted in English.

Duration of assignment: The successful candidate will work under a one (1) year renewable contract based on competence and approval by the Ministry.

Facilities to be provided: MoLSA will provide the office facilities, essential utilities, office services, stationery and office supplies and use of a computer and a printer.

Location of assignment: The duty station is in Kismayo, Jubbaland State of Somalia. The State Liaison Officer will be based at the Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs or Baxnaano Offices.

Southwest State Liaison Officer is required by the Federal Government of Somalia (FGS) to support implementation of a World Bank-funded project, Building Opportunities and Outcomes in Social Protection and Youth Employment (BOOST You) (P507443). The selected candidate will work for the government’s National Social Protection Program (Baxnaano), established in 2019 and housed at the Federal Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs (MoLSA).

Project Overview

The project development objective of Building Opportunities and Outcomes in Social Protection and Youth Employment (BOOST-YOU) is to enhance economic opportunities and strengthen resilience of the poor and vulnerable. The project directly contributes to strengthening Somalia’s social protection system, expanding coverage through its support to the jobs agenda and building greater resilience to shocks through robust adaptive social protection mechanisms. The project applies an integrated approach that moves beneficiaries along a continuum from protection to production.

The project aims to support the poor and most vulnerable of the population by providing targeted interventions to improve their resilience and prepare for better jobs tomorrow, while providing job opportunities now by addressing key barriers to better income-generating opportunities. The project will reach about 206,000 households in particularly climate-exposed areas, which is equivalent to over 1.2 million individual beneficiaries.

The program supports poor and vulnerable households through following components:

Component 1: Connecting Youth and Women to Better Jobs Today: Supports 28,000 youth (60% women & 5% disable persons) in urban areas with limited job opportunities and prolonged periods of inactivity, benefit from economic inclusion activities (wage and self-employment activities). contributing directly creating jobs and strengthening households’ resilience.

Component 2: Investing in People for Better Jobs Tomorrow: The component will deliver regular cash transfers to 50,000 of the poorest households to meet basic needs, enhance climate-challenged food security, and prevent negative coping strategies during climate shocks, which in turn helps safeguard the human capital necessary for productive participation in the labor force. Approximately 10,000 shock affected poor and vulnerable households will be supported with emergency cash transfers as part of a contingent financing arrangement in case of climate shocks. 30,000 pregnant women and mothers with children under two will receive health- and nutrition-linked co-responsibility cash transfers (CCTs) to promote maternal and child health, reduce malnutrition, and improve early childhood development, strengthening the human capital necessary for future workforce productivity whilst mitigating adverse climate impacts. An early response-Health and Nutrition CCT will support 83,000 shock affected households with pregnant women and mothers with children under two to reduce the prevalence of significant acute malnutrition and infant mortality in drought affected prioritized districts. An education CCT program will target 5,000 children from the poorest and most climate-affected households, helping build the foundation required for long-term employability by increasing school enrollment and attendance.

Component 3: Adaptive Social Protection Systems and Project Management: Supports enhancement of an adaptive social protection system, the National Socio-Economic Survey and project management including institutional capacity building for MoLSA. The objective of this support is to create a robust, efficient, and responsive social protection infrastructure. By strengthening institutional capacity, enhancing data management, strengthening the delivery system and registering the population in the USR, this component lays the foundation for sustainable and effective social protection and multisectoral poverty targeted investments. Under this component National Socio-economic Survey (NSES) will register 12 million people in Somalia in the USR collecting socio-economic data to inform targeting for pro-poor programs in the country. The component also provides support for effective project management, capacity building and oversight of project activities.

Appendix 1 - Terms of Reference

Terms of Reference

Targeted Assessment and Amendment of Fiji’s Electricity Act 2017 to Enable Private Sector Participation in Renewable Electricity Generation

1.0 Background

Energy is a key driver of economic growth and social development in Fiji. Ensuring energy security and reliable access is increasingly important given external shocks such as pandemics, global geopolitical disruptions, and climate-driven natural disasters. Fiji’s energy transition requires strengthened sector planning led by Government in coordination with sector stakeholders (including Energy Fiji Limited (EFL), the Fijian Competition and Consumer Commission (FCCC), and private investors) to ensure that enabling legislation, regulations, and policies support investment, accelerate renewable energy (RE) deployment, and strengthen climate resilience and energy efficiency in electricity infrastructure.

Fiji has committed to a low-carbon development pathway and aims to transition its electricity sector toward renewable energy. Fiji’s updated Nationally Determined Contributions (2020) and the SDG 7 Roadmap (2022) reflect the national ambition to increase renewable generation capacity and progress toward a predominantly renewable electricity system by 2036. Fiji’s electricity access rate in 2024 was approximately 97%, and renewable energy contributed an estimated 51% of generation excluding bioenergy.

While renewable technology costs have declined significantly over the past decade and private sector interest in investment is growing, private participation remains constrained by gaps in policy implementation and by legal and regulatory barriers affecting market access and the bankability of Independent Power Producer (IPP) projects.

The Electricity Act 2017 was enacted to modernize the sector, corporatize the former Fiji Electricity Authority into EFL, and confirm FCCC as the independent economic regulator. However, private investment in renewable energy has remained limited, and the legal and regulatory framework continues to present barriers to achieving Fiji’s energy transition goals.

2.0 Rationale

To strengthen the enabling environment for Fiji’s energy transition, the Government of Fiji (GoF), in partnership with the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA) through the Small Island Developing States (SIDS) Lighthouses Initiative (LHI), undertook a gap analysis study titled “Assessment of Legislative and Regulatory Frameworks for a Just and Inclusive Energy Transition.”

The Gap Analysis examined Fiji’s legal, regulatory and institutional framework for electricity generation, transmission and supply. It identified barriers and uncertainties that may constrain the deployment of renewable energy and private sector participation in electricity generation. The study found that, while the Electricity Act 2017 allows IPPs to participate in electricity generation, the existing framework does not provide sufficient clarity, predictability and certainty regarding how private renewable energy participants can enter, operate and invest in Fiji’s electricity sector.

The Gap Analysis identified several areas requiring further assessment and possible legislative or regulatory reform, including:

  • unclear or limited recognition of renewable energy, Independent Power Producers, distributed energy resources, energy storage and other emerging forms of private renewable electricity generation;
  • dependence on negotiated Power Purchase Agreements between EFL and Independent Power Producers, without a sufficiently clear and predictable framework for pricing, risk allocation, negotiation timelines, approval and dispute resolution;
  • the need for clearer arrangements for procuring new renewable electricity generation, including assessment of competitive and other procurement approaches suitable for Fiji;

This assignment will build upon the relevant findings of the Gap Analysis and undertake a targeted assessment of the provisions of the Act and associated instruments that affect private sector participation in renewable electricity generation. The assessment will examine the legal and regulatory arrangements affecting IPPs, distributed generation, self-generation, storage and mini grids. It will also identify whether the barriers to private participation should be addressed through amendments to the Act, subsidiary regulations, license conditions, standard agreements, procurement arrangements or improved implementation.

The assignment is not intended to constitute a comprehensive review, redrafting or replacement of the Electricity Act 2017. The assessment shall focus on priority provisions and arrangements that materially affect private sector participation in renewable electricity generation and the enabling environment required for such participation.

In this context, the Government of Fiji, supported by the World Bank Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP) for the Fiji Energy Transformation Project, seeks to identify and develop targeted, evidence-based amendments to the Electricity Act 2017 and any related reforms required to establish a transparent, predictable and workable legislative environment for private sector participation in renewable electricity generation.

The proposed reforms shall support renewable energy development while safeguarding affordability, system reliability, security of supply, consumer interests and the financial and operational sustainability of Fiji’s electricity system.

3.0 Objective of the Assignment

Building upon the findings of the Gap Analysis Study, the primary objective of this assignment is to undertake a targeted assessment of the Electricity Act 2017 and relevant associated instruments to identify priority legal and regulatory barriers to private sector participation in renewable electricity generation, and to develop targeted, evidence-based amendments and complementary reform measures to address those barriers.

The assignment shall identify the appropriate legal, regulatory, contractual, institutional or administrative mechanism for addressing each priority barrier and shall distinguish matters requiring amendment to the Electricity Act 2017 from those that may be addressed through subsidiary regulations, licence conditions, regulatory decisions, technical codes, standard agreements, guidelines or improved implementation and enforcement.

The assignment shall support a clear, transparent and predictable framework for participation by Independent Power Producers, distributed energy resources, self-generators, energy storage providers, mini-grid operators and other relevant renewable energy participants, while safeguarding electricity affordability, system reliability, security of supply, consumer interests, and the financial and operational sustainability of Fiji’s electricity system.

The specific objectives of the consultancy are to:

  • Build upon the relevant findings of the Gap Analysis Study to identify priority legal and regulatory barriers to private sector participation in renewable electricity generation.
  • Undertake a targeted assessment of the Electricity Act 2017 and relevant associated instruments affecting Independent Power Producers, distributed energy resources, self-generators, storage providers and mini-grid operators.
  • Identify priority barriers to private renewable electricity generation, including those relating to but not limited to licensing and exemptions, self-supply, grid access and interconnection, electricity procurement, Power Purchase Agreements, pricing arrangements, risk allocation and dispute resolution.
  • Assess proportionate reform options for addressing the identified barriers, including improved implementation of existing regulatory powers, negotiated PPAs, competitive procurement and other arrangements appropriate to Fiji’s market size, institutional capacity, affordability requirements, grid conditions and security-of-supply needs.
  • Determine which priority barriers require amendments to the Electricity Act 2017, and which may be addressed through subsidiary regulations, license conditions, regulatory decisions, technical codes, standard agreements, guidelines or improved implementation and enforcement.
  • Prepare targeted legislative amendments and a concise implementation roadmap setting out the actions, sequencing, responsible institutions, indicative timeframes, transitional arrangements, and consequential changes required to implement the proposed amendments.

4.0 Scope of Works

The consultant shall undertake a thorough and targeted assessment of the Electricity Act 2017 and relevant associated instruments to identify provisions that may constrain, discourage, or create uncertainty for private sector participation in renewable electricity generation. The assignment shall be informed by the findings of the Assessment of Legislative and Regulatory Frameworks for a Just and Inclusive Energy Transition in Fiji. However, the consultant shall independently scrutinise the Electricity Act 2017 and shall not be limited to the barriers identified in the Gap Analysis.

The consultant shall distinguish between matters requiring amendments to the Electricity Act 2017 and matters that may be addressed through subsidiary regulations, licence conditions, regulatory decisions, technical codes, standard agreements, guidelines, or improved implementation and enforcement.

Task 1: Inception and Targeted Legal, Policy and Regulatory Assessment

The consultant shall:

  • Prepare an Inception Report setting out the proposed methodology, workplan, stakeholder consultation plan, information requirements, and schedule for completing the assignment.
  • Undertake a thorough assessment of the Electricity Act 2017 to identify provisions that may constrain, discourage, or create uncertainty for private sector participation in renewable electricity generation.
  • Examine the Electricity Regulations 2019, relevant electricity licences, and applicable regulatory instruments only to the extent necessary to understand how the relevant provisions of the Act operate in practice.
  • Assess the legal, policy and regulatory treatment of Independent Power Producers, distributed energy resources, self-generators, energy storage providers, mini-grid operators, and other relevant private renewable electricity participants.
  • Examine priority matters relating to definitions, licensing and exemptions, self-supply, distributed generation, EFL’s exclusive rights, grid access and interconnection, electricity procurement, Power Purchase Agreements, electricity purchase-price arrangements, institutional responsibilities, dispute resolution, compliance, and enforcement.
  • Identify whether each barrier arises from the Electricity Act itself or from subsidiary instruments, licence conditions, regulatory practices, commercial arrangements, institutional responsibilities, or implementation and enforcement.
  • Prepare a Legal Issues and Barriers Matrix identifying the relevant provision, the barrier identified, its practical effect on private sector participation, and the appropriate mechanism for addressing it.

Task 2: Targeted Stakeholder Consultations

The consultant shall:

  • Conduct targeted consultations with DOE, FCCC, EFL, relevant Government ministries and agencies (the Ministry of Finance, Office of the Attorney-General, Ministry of Environment and Climate Change, relevant land and planning authorities), existing and prospective IPPs, and other relevant stakeholders, e.g. consumer and community representatives.
  • Obtain practical evidence on barriers affecting licensing, grid access and interconnection, electricity procurement, PPA negotiations, pricing certainty, project financing, regulatory approvals, and dispute resolution.
  • Determine whether the identified barriers arise from the legislation itself or from its administration, interpretation, implementation, or enforcement.
  • Seek stakeholder views on possible legislative and regulatory responses and their likely implications for private investment, EFL, consumers, electricity affordability, system reliability, and security of supply.
  • Prepare a concise Stakeholder Consultation Report and Consultation Matrix setting out the principal issues raised, areas of agreement and disagreement, and how stakeholder input informed the proposed reforms.

The consultations shall build upon the wider stakeholder consultation process previously undertaken under the Gap Analysis and shall focus on obtaining updated information and evidence relevant to this targeted assignment.

Task 3: Assessment of Reform and Procurement Options

Based on the legal, policy and regulatory assessment and stakeholder consultations, the consultant shall:

  1. Identify and compare proportionate options for addressing the priority barriers to private sector participation in renewable electricity generation. Depending on the nature of each barrier, the measures may include, but are not limited to:

a. improved administration, interpretation, and enforcement of existing powers.

b. targeted amendments to the Electricity Act 2017.

c. amendments to subsidiary regulations or licence conditions.

d. clearer regulatory guidance, technical codes, or standard agreements.

e. strengthened arrangements for negotiated Power Purchase Agreements.

f. competitive procurement for suitable categories of renewable electricity generation; or

g. an appropriate combination of these measures.

 

  1. Recommend other measures where supported by the assessment and identify the most appropriate legislative, regulatory, contractual, institutional, or administrative mechanism for addressing each priority barrier.
  2. Assess options for establishing a transparent and fit-for-purpose renewable energy procurement framework, including competitive and other appropriate procurement approaches, taking into account Fiji’s market size, institutional capacity, consumer affordability, investor confidence and project bankability, system reliability and security of supply, and the appropriate allocation of risks among Government, EFL and private-sector developers.
  3. Where a renewable energy procurement framework is recommended, identify the necessary legal and regulatory arrangements, institutional roles, core procurement principles, standard documentation requirements, and appropriate legal instruments for implementation.
  4. Provide drafting instructions for any supporting procurement instruments requiring subsequent development. The consultant shall not be required to prepare complete procurement regulations, bidding documents, a model PPA, or a detailed auction design under this assignment.
  5. Assess whether different arrangements may be appropriate for utility-scale IPPs, distributed energy resources, commercial and industrial self-generation, energy storage, mini-grids, and other categories of renewable electricity generation. The structure options include but not limited to PPPs, SPV and JV financial model concessions, and other private-investment structures, and compare these with conventional IPP arrangements.
  6. Consider the likely implications of the principal reform options for private sector participation, EFL’s financial and operational sustainability, consumer affordability, whole-of-system costs, grid integration, system reliability, and security of supply.
  7. Recommend the most appropriate and proportionate reform approach, or combination of approaches, for Fiji, supported by clear evidence and reasoning. Competitive procurement, including auctions, shall be assessed as one possible approach and shall not be presumed to be appropriate for every technology, project type, or project scale.
  8. The assessment of renewable energy procurement options shall be undertaken at a strategic, legal, regulatory and institutional level. It shall identify and compare procurement approaches appropriate to Fiji and recommend the preferred framework and associated legal and institutional arrangements. The assignment shall not require detailed electricity system modelling, detailed financial or tariff modelling, detailed auction design, preparation of bidding documents, preparation of a model Power Purchase Agreement, or development of complete procurement regulations.

Task 4: Targeted Legislative Amendments and Implementation Roadmap

Based on the preferred reform approach, the consultant shall:

  1. Prepare targeted amendments to the Electricity Act 2017, in the form of a draft Electricity (Amendment) Bill or equivalent legislative drafting document, clearly identifying the specific provisions to be inserted, amended or repealed, together with concise explanatory notes setting out the rationale and legal effect of each amendment. The amendments shall be limited to priority barriers identified through the assignment and shall not constitute a comprehensive redraft or replacement of the Act.
  2. Ensure that the proposed amendments provide clear and proportionate arrangements for relevant categories and scales of private renewable electricity generation.
  3. Address, where required, barriers relating to licensing, exemptions, self-generation, grid access and interconnection, electricity procurement, PPAs, purchase-price arrangements from private generators, dispute resolution, compliance, and enforcement.
  4. Clarify any institutional powers, functions and responsibilities necessary to implement the proposed amendments relating to private sector participation in renewable electricity generation.
  5. Include any enabling powers necessary for subsequent regulations, licence conditions, procurement rules, technical codes, standard agreements or regulatory guidelines required to implement the proposed amendments.
  6. Ensure that the proposed amendments retain sufficient flexibility to accommodate future developments in renewable energy technologies, energy storage, project structures, and business models.
  7. Ensure that the proposed amendments safeguard electricity affordability, consumer interests, system reliability, security of supply, and the financial and operational sustainability of Fiji’s electricity system.
  8. Identify consequential changes required to the Electricity Regulations 2019, electricity licences, regulatory instruments, technical codes, standard agreements, guidelines, or other associated instruments.
  9. Present the proposed amendments and recommendations to DOE and selected stakeholders through a validation session and incorporate comments where appropriate.
  10. Prepare a matrix recording significant comments received and explaining how they were addressed.
  11. Finalise the targeted amendments and explanatory notes following the validation process.
  12. Prepare a concise implementation roadmap identifying the required actions, sequencing, responsible institutions, indicative timeframes, approval requirements, transitional arrangements, consequential changes to associated instruments, and priority follow-on activities.

5.0 Environmental and Social Considerations

GOVERNMENT OF THE REPUBLIC OF MALAWI

 

 

 

Ministry of Health and Sanitation

 

 

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

 

CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRM SELECTION

Name of Project              : Malawi Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and

                                            Resilience Program

Project ID No                   : P505187

Assignment Title              : Provision of Consultancy Services to

                                      develop guidelines and architectural drawings for

                                      climate resilient and energy efficient health care

                                      infrastructure in various sites around Malawi

Reference No.                  : MW-MOH-565052-CS-QCBS

Date of Issue                     : 28th September, 2026

 

 

 

 

  1. BACKGROUND

 

The Government of Malawi through the Ministry of Health and Sanitation is implementing the Malawi Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and Resilience (MHEPRR) project.  The project is financed through the International Development Association (IDA) and Global Financing Facility (GFF) at an estimated budget of US$60 Million.  The project aims at consolidating efforts from the World Bank and development partners to provide relief and strengthen health systems against economic shocks, climate disasters, and public health emergencies, aligning with the Government's focus on Pandemic Preparedness and Response after COVID-19.  The expected duration for implementation of the Malawi Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and Resilience (MHEPRR) project is 5 years with a close date of December 2029. This five-year initiative is aimed at strengthening the country’s ability to respond to health crises, including those intensified by climate change.

 

Alignment with HSSP III and the Resilience Framework

In direct response to these vulnerabilities and in alignment with the Health Sector Strategic Plan III (HSSP III), the Ministry of Health and Sanitation is prioritizing the construction of specialized climate resilient health care infrastructure as a fundamental pillar of national resilience. This initiative represents a strategic shift from centralized care to a decentralized “Surge Ready” model. By establishing high standard climate resilient health care infrastructure in geographically vulnerable areas, the Ministry aims to bridge the critical gap between primary care and overstretched central facilities.

 

Project Scope

 

Under the first phase of the MHEPRR project, the Ministry is utilizing funding from the World Bank to conduct comprehensive technical assessments for the construction of these facilities in selected disaster-prone sites. This includes the development of standardized architectural designs and technical specifications that can be adapted to the specific climate change related risks of each location and conducting Environmental and Social Assessments for the proposed sites.

 

 

  1. PURPOSE AND OBJECTIVES OF THE ASSIGNMENT

 

The purpose of this assignment is to engage a qualified multidisciplinary consulting firm to undertake the planning and design of standardized, cost effective, modular, climate resilient and energy efficient functional community hospitals to be constructed across various sites in Malawi.

 

The consulting firm will provide comprehensive architectural and engineering design services, including site specific adaptation for multistory and modular structures to be used by the Ministry of Health and Sanitation.

 

 

2.1. Specific objectives

The specific objectives of the assignment will include the following:

 

  1. To conduct a comprehensive pre-design assessment and feasibility study for each proposed site to inform the planning and design of the community hospitals. The findings of this assessment shall guide the functional brief, space requirements, service scope, phasing strategy and overall design approach to ensure the proposed facilities are responsive to local health service needs and site conditions.
  2. To prepare coordinated architectural and engineering designs for community hospitals to be constructed across multiple districts while remaining adaptable to site specific conditions. This will result in complete and integrated construction drawings, technical specifications and bill of quantities that are sufficient.
  3. To prepare blank Bills of quantities and costed bills of quantities that will lead to cost estimates
  4. To prepare complete tender documentation per site which will be used to procure a contractor to execute the works on the sites.

 

  1. Conduct Environmental and Social Impact Assessments (ESIA) and prepare a report

 

  1. Prepare comprehensive Bidding Documents for tendering in accordance with World Bank requirements and Government of Malawi procurement regulations, ensuring the inclusion of an Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP) from the approved ESIA report to be added to the Bills of Quantities for the entire proposed hospital

 

 

  1. DETAILS OF THE ASSIGNMENT

 

The consulting firm will come up with designs for various sites and associated Bills of Quantities that will be packaged according to the needs of each site. Geotechnical and topographical surveys will have to be carried out to ascertain specific site conditions and disaster-prone areas. Social and environmental assessments will be carried out and the key findings or parameters to be considered in the structural designs and the development of bills of quantities.

 

 

  1. SCOPE OF CONSULTANCY WORK

 

The consultancy will conduct the following actions:

 

(a) Site Surveys

 Making an initial visit to the site and carrying out an appraisal of the site and existing buildings

 

  • Conduct detailed site surveys to assess existing physical conditions, topography, geotechnical surveys, utilities, environmental and social considerations, access routes, and any site constraints.
  • Carry out geotechnical investigations, including soil testing and analysis and provide recommendations for foundation systems and structural considerations based on ground conditions.
  • Prepare a site assessment report outlining findings and implications for design.
  • Environmental and social assessment: identify existing natural features such as water and air quality,  wildlife habitats, forests, pre-existing hazardous waste, soil stability and natural disaster risks etc. to be affected and any other natural resources and habitats to be preserved.

 

(c) Design development and cost estimations

 

  • Prepare conceptual, schematic, and detailed architectural and engineering designs.
  • Develop spatial layouts in accordance with Community hospital infrastructure standards.
  • Provide detailed cost estimates at each design stage to ensure alignment.
  • Revise designs as necessary based on stakeholder feedback and regulatory requirements.

 

(d) Regulatory and Standards compliance:

  • Ensure full compliance with guidelines issued by the World Health Organization (WHO), particularly in relation to spatial planning and healthcare facility requirements under the Safe Hospitals Initiative Guidelines (SHIG).
  • Obtain or support the acquisition of necessary approvals and clearances from relevant authorities.

(e) Environmental and Social Assessment (ESA):

  • Prepare a project brief to be submitted to the MEPA upon client review
  • Undertake ESIA in accordance with the provisions of international policies and laws such as the World Bank Environmental and Social standards, policies as well as national policies, legislations and regulations. Provide a concise description of the biophysical characteristics and the social-economic environment status of each site. The assessment will also include Occupational, Health and Safety considerations, high-level assessment of waste,noise and dust impacts,air quality, climate change and risk assessment.
  •  
  • Prepare ESIA report for each site and a consolidated assessment report which will feed into the main report.
  1. DESIGN PRINCIPLES

 

•         Patient-centred and clinically functional planning.

•         Universal accessibility and inclusive design.

•         Infection prevention and control.

•         Fire and life safety.

•         Climate resilience and disaster risk reduction.

•         Energy and water efficiency.

•         Low-maintenance and locally supportable systems.

•         Appropriate security and controlled circulation.

•         Provision for future expansion.

•         Whole-life cost/value-for-money considerations.

 

6.       DELIVERABLES

 

The output from the consultancy will include an inception report, architectural designs, engineering drawings, bills of quantities, cost estimates based on bills of quantities, tender documents, a masterplan for each site, an environmental and social assessment report for each site, consolidated ESIA report based on terms of reference issued by MEPA  and a comprehensive final design report. The Secretariat intends to engage a qualified consulting firm to develop new multimedia content where explanation gaps exist and to transform selected approved learning materials into concise animated videos. The videos will incorporate infographics, accurate data visualizations, professional voice-over narration, captions, and transcripts, and will be suitable for the EAC Learning Management System, websites, and mobile access.

The assignment will be completed within a maximum of ten weeks from contract commencement. The principal deliverables will include an inception report and production plan; scripts, storyboards, and visual style; a pilot video; a complete draft video package; and final master, LMS/mobile, caption, transcript, thumbnail, editable-source-file, asset/licence, and completion-report packages.

3. SHORTLISTING CRITERIA

  • Specialized technical capability: Team Composition and Expertise- Do not provide the CVs of the staff. Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage. Demonstrated capability in animation, instructional design, infographics, data visualization, professional voice-over, captions/transcripts, accessibility, audiovisual quality assurance, editable-source-file handover, and copyright/licensing management.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

 

 

Organisation of the Eastern Caribbean States Commission (OECSC)

Caribbean Efficient and Green-Energy Buildings Project

Grant No.: IDA-E4140

Assignment Title: Investment-grade audits and detailed design of Energy Efficiency Measures (EEM) and Distributed Photovoltaic (DPV) systems in Public Buildings and Facilities in Grenada, Saint Lucia and Guyana.

Reference No.: LC-OECS COMMISSION-554122-CS-QCBS

Participating Countries: Grenada, Saint Lucia and Guyana

 

The Organisation of the Eastern Caribbean States Commission (OECSC) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Caribbean Efficient and Green-Energy Buildings Project. The OECSC intends to apply part of the proceeds for Investment-grade audits and detailed design of Energy Efficiency Measures (EEM) and Distributed Photovoltaic (DPV) systems in Public Buildings and Facilities in Grenada, Saint Lucia and Guyana.

 

The objective of this assignment is to conduct Investment Grade Audits (IGAs), compliant with ASHRAE Level 3 standards or equivalent, for selected public buildings in Grenada, Guyana, and Saint Lucia, in order to identify, evaluate, and prioritize Energy Efficiency Measures (EEMs) and Distributed Photovoltaic (DPV) systems for implementation.

The assignment will support the preparation of investment-ready interventions for approximately 250 public buildings through:

 

  1. Detailed assessment of current building energy performance;
  2. Identification and technical evaluation of cost-effective EEMs and DPV options;
  3. Economic and financial analysis of EEMs and DPV proposed measures, including lifecycle costs, savings, payback, IRR, and NPV;
  4. Preparation of detailed engineering designs, technical specifications, drawings, and Bills of Quantities (BOQs);
  5. Assessment of environmental and social (E&S) risks associated with the proposed measures in accordance with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), national regulations, and applicable project safeguards instruments; and
  6. Development of inputs required for procurement including bidding documents for the proposed measures;

 

The IGAs will be undertaken under a 2-year Framework Agreement, in the first instance, with distinct batches of buildings addressed under call-off assignments expected to last 6-8 months per batch.

 

The OECS Commission now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. In the assessment of submissions, consideration will be given to technical competence, qualifications and experience, and local and regional experience on similar assignments.

 

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

 

The shortlisting criteria are:

 

  1. A firm with relevant international (experience outside the country where the firm is based) project experience for at least ten (10) years. Relevant technical experience would include programs related to EEMs and DPVs in buildings (especially public buildings).
  2. At least Five (5) years of experience conducting ASHRAE Level 3 or equivalent energy audits in public buildings and having completed at least 3 assignments covering a combined minimum of 50 buildings.
  3. At least 3 completed projects involving identification and technical evaluation of EEMs with a minimum contract value of USD $170,000.
  4. At least 2 completed projects involving design or assessment of distributed solar PV systems with a minimum contract value of USD $100,000.
