1. BACKGROUND

The Ministry of Finance has received financing from the World Bank and a grant from the European Union toward the cost of the Construction of a New Runway and Other facilities for Plaine Corail Airport, Rodrigues and intends to apply part of the proceeds towards recruitment of Individual Consultancy for Gender Based Violence (GBV) Specialist

2. OBJECTIVE OF THE ASSIGNMENT 

The GBV/SEA/SH Specialist will be responsible for leading, coordinating, and overseeing the implementation of all GBV/SEA/SH prevention, mitigation, and response measures under the project. The Specialist will ensure that GBV/SEA/SH risks are systematically identified, assessed, mitigated, and appropriately responded to throughout all phases of project implementation, in full alignment with the project’s SEA/SH Action Plan, the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), and applicable national laws and policies

3.0       BRIEF SCOPE OF THE ASSIGNMENT

  • Serve as the technical lead for the project's SEA/SH risk management strategy, owning the implementation and periodic update of the SEA/SH Action Plan (including indicators, budgets, and timelines) based on evolving project activities and risk assessments.
  • Support the PIU Social Specialist in integrating SEA/SH risks and mitigation measures into all relevant Environmental and Social project documentation, including the C-ESMP, SEP, LMP, and contractor E&S requirements.
  • Assist in developing and keeping current the project's Accountability and Response Framework, documenting procedures for handling SEA/SH allegations and ensuring coherence with referral protocols and the Grievance Mechanism.
  • Identify emerging GBV/SEA/SH risks during construction and operational phases and propose updated mitigation measures to the PIU.
  • Ensure that all project-related workers, including civil works contractors and sub-contractors, have adopted and are implementing appropriate Codes of Conduct (CoC) that explicitly address SEA/SH.
  • Establish SEA/SH-sensitive channels within the project Grievance Mechanism — covering both community-based and worker-facing pathways — that are safe, confidential, and ethical.
  • Mobilize and coordinate GBV expertise (including the GBV NGO) to design and deliver SEA/SH training programs for all project actors — PIU staff, civil works contractors, supervision consultants, and ARL/AML management — tailored to each audience

4. INVITATION FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

The Airports of Mauritius Co. Ltd now invites eligible candidates (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

REPUBLIC OF THE GAMBIA

The Gambia Water and Sanitation Project (WASAP)

Project ID: P513113

Assignment Title:

Consultancy Services for Feasibility Studies, Detailed Engineering Design, Procurement Support, Construction Supervision, and Defects Liability Support for Urban Water Supply Systems in Kombo East and Urban Sanitation Infrastructure in Kotu and Banjul

Reference No.: GM-NAWEC-565968-CS-QCBS

The Republic of The Gambia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Gambia Water and Sanitation Project (WASAP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for Feasibility Studies, Detailed Engineering Design, Procurement Support, Construction Supervision, and Defects Liability Support for Urban Water Supply Systems in Kombo East and Urban Sanitation Infrastructure in Kotu and Banjul.

The Greater Banjul Area is the country’s principal urban and economic center. Urban water services face major challenges including production constraints, intermittent supply, ageing infrastructure, limited storage capacity, and high levels of non-revenue water. Similarly, sanitation services in Banjul and Kotu are constrained by deteriorated sewerage assets, underperforming wastewater treatment facilities, and inadequate fecal sludge management infrastructure.  WASAP will support the Government of The Gambia in addressing these challenges through investments aimed at improving service coverage, reliability, resilience, and sustainability of water supply and sanitation services.

The assignment will support the preparation and implementation of priority investments in urban water supply and urban sanitation infrastructure, including:

  • Urban water supply investments in Kombo East and Brikama East comprising boreholes, treatment facilities, storage reservoirs, transmission pipelines, distribution networks, household connections, SCADA systems, and power supply facilities; and
  • Urban sanitation investments including rehabilitation and expansion of wastewater and sewerage infrastructure in Kotu and Banjul, fecal sludge treatment facilities, pumping stations, and associated infrastructure.

The consulting services will be undertaken in five phases:

  • Prepare design calculations, drawings, technical specifications, cost estimates, bills of quantities, and O&M documentation.
  • Prepare procurement-ready engineering packages.

Phase 3: Procurement Support

  • Prepare complete bidding documents and technical specifications.
  • Participate in pre-bid meetings and site visits.
  • Provide support during bid evaluation and contract award processes.
  • Respond to technical clarifications and prepare addenda where required.

Phase 4: Construction Supervision and Contract Administration

  • Supervise construction works and administer contracts.
  • Monitor quality assurance, environmental and social compliance, occupational health and safety, cost and schedule performance.
  • Review contractor submissions and oversee testing and commissioning.
  • Support handover and completion.

Phase 5: Defects Liability Support

  • Conduct inspections during the defect’s liability period.
  • Verify correction of defects.
  • Support final completion and contract close-out.

The estimated duration of the assignment is 46.5 months, including feasibility studies, design, procurement support, construction supervision, and defects liability support.

The SADC Secretariat, through the Regional Statistics Project (RSP) (P175731), has received grant financing from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank. The Project Development Objective is to strengthen the institutional capacity of SADC to produce, disseminate and use quality statistics while increasing regional harmonisation and collaboration. Under the Project, SADC is implementing Component 1: Harmonisation, Quality and Dissemination of Core Social and Economic Statistics.

 

In view of the above, the SADC Secretariat is undertaking several interventions aimed at strengthening the SADC Regional Statistical System (SRSS) and enhancing the production, quality, harmonisation, dissemination and use of regional statistics. These interventions include technical assistance and capacity building activities in priority statistical areas, including poverty statistics, statistical software and data processing, survey methodologies, national accounts, environment and climate change statistics, statistical communication, quality assurance and harmonised regional statistical guidelines.

 

The SADC Secretariat intends to apply part of the proceeds of the grant towards the consulting services to revise and update the SADC Harmonised Consumer price Index Methods and Procedures in SADC region, in support of the objectives of the Regional Statistics Project.

REFERENCE NO.:                                       SO-MOCT-FGS-575152-CS-INDV

APPLICATION DEADLINE DATE:              October 15, 2026, at 1.00pm, Eastern Africa Time (EAT)

 

BACKGROUND:

The Federal Republic of Somalia, situated on the Horn of Africa, faces deep economic and environmental vulnerabilities. The country’s economy depends heavily on remittances— accounting for over 31 percent of GDP—and on traditional livelihoods such as pastoralism, which supports about half of Somalia’s 16.3 million people and contributes around 60 percent of GDP. However, climate shocks, including floods, droughts, and locust infestations since 2019, have devastated livelihoods and left 5.2 million people in need of humanitarian aid. With nearly 70 percent of the population living below the international poverty line, poverty and food insecurity remain critical challenges. Somalia’s digital infrastructure is underdeveloped, further constraining economic growth and regional integration.

Through World Bank’s support, The Eastern Africa Regional Digital Integration operation (EA-

RDIP)’ (2023-2028) is being prepared to address connectivity needs for countries in the Horn of Africa region. The proposed program aims to advance the regional integration of digital markets Eastern Africa through supporting cross-border connectivity, harmonization of data and ecommerce regulations and policies, and removal of trade barriers, with the vision of establishing a Single Digital Market (SDM). It is proposed for the project components to follow the SDM framework and for participating countries (Ethiopia, Somalia, South Sudan in phase 1) to tailor each component for its investment and technical assistance needs. Specifically, Somalia’s $80 million EA-RDIP investment will focus on expanding broadband access, bridging infrastructure gaps, and aligning digital regulations with regional standards—laying the groundwork for greater economic inclusion and integration within the Horn of Africa. The EA-RDIP project has four components, as briefly described below:

  1. Component 1. Connectivity Market Development and Integration.
  2. Component 2. Data Market Development and Integration.
  3. Component 3. Online Market Development and integration.
  4. Component 4. Project Management and implementation.

A Project Implementation Unit (PIU) is set up at the Ministry of Communications and Technology (MoCT), which is responsible for overall implementation, fiduciary and Environment and Social Framework (ESF) compliance for the project. The PIU is supported by technical committees (TCs) bringing together key Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs) and federal member states (FMS), reports to a Project Steering Committee (PSC), and coordinates with the regional PIUs at the East African Community (EAC) and the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD). To support the effective and efficient delivery of EA-RDIP activities, MoCT intends to hire a highly motivated and dynamic Communications Specialist within the PIU to develop and implement the project communication strategy and action plan, expand the visibility of the project and its development results, and ensure that the project is branded in a way that is consistent with its intended development outcomes.

OBJECTIVE OF THE ASSIGNMENT:  

The Communications Specialist will work with the PIU team to design and manage all aspects of internal and external project communications, including the EA-RDIP Communication Strategy and annual Communication Plans, project branding and messaging in English and Somali, the project website and social media, multimedia content, media engagement and community feedback. He/she will develop high-quality knowledge products and learning content, such as data visualizations, success stories and case studies, coordinate communication with the regional PIUs at EAC and IGAD, and provide demand-driven communication training to project beneficiaries. The Communications Specialist will report to the PIU Project Coordinator.

SHORTLISTING CRITERIA:  

The shortlisting criteria for PIU Communications Specialist position are set out below.

  1. A minimum of a Master’s degree or equivalent higher education in communications, journalism, public relations, social sciences or international relations.
  2. Minimum of 7 years of working experience in developing and implementing communication strategies, with relevant experience in mass media, journalism or multimedia production and communications for a public-sector institution at national or international level.
  3. Experience in developing and implementing project or institutional branding and messaging, and in managing social media content and presence on appropriate platforms and messaging services.
  4. Demonstrated experience producing digital and multimedia content (videos, photography, infographics, audio) and managing project websites, including content management, social media and analytics tools.
  5. Experience leading similar assignment(s) in Somalia or similar contexts, with knowledge of public and private media houses in Somalia, and experience coordinating communication with regional or multi-country institutions, preferably in a regional integration program.
  6. Excellent command of written and spoken English, with excellent communication and negotiation skills. Knowledge of the Somali language (spoken and written) and experience with World Bank-financed projects, including the Environment and Social Framework and citizen engagement requirements, is an advantage.

DURATION OF THE ASSIGNMENT: The PIU Communications Specialist will be engaged for a period of one (1) year subject to renewal on an annual basis based on satisfactory performance, assessed against the performance indicators in the ToR, and availability of funds.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION

Republic of Serbia

Serbia Inclusive Primary Education Improvement Project (IPEIP)

Project ID No. P181557

Assignment Title:

Pedagogical and Methodological Support and Implementation of the National Assessments and Trainings

Reference No. SER-IPEIP-QCBS-CS-26-16 

The Republic of Serbia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Serbia Inclusive Primary Education Improvement Project (IPEIP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments for consulting services to be procured under this project.

Scope of Services

The objective of this assignment is to provide the Ministry of Education (MoE) and the Education Quality and Evaluation (IEQE) with comprehensive pedagogical, methodological, psychometric, organizational, and technical support for the preparation, piloting, implementation, analysis, and reporting of the national assessment in primary education.

The assignment is intended to ensure that the agreed conceptual and methodological framework is translated into a clearly planned, feasible, and standardized national assessment cycle capable of producing reliable data on student achievement and supporting the use of those data for improving education policies and school practice.

The consultant shall provide support in the development of the assessment methodology, assessment instruments, an item bank, test forms, and contextual questionnaires. The support shall also include the preparation of procedures for sampling, communication with schools, administration of the assessment, quality assurance, secure handling of assessment materials, and the protection of personal data.

The Consultant shall work closely with the IEQE and the Project Management Unit (PMU) team within the MoE in completing the following main tasks:

  • Development of Methodology and Assessment Instruments, including the national assessment concept and frameworks, assessment instruments, item banks, test forms and contextual questionnaires, accessibility arrangements, as well as methodological and psychometric requirements and professional verification inputs for the Grade 7 online assessment solution;
  • Logistics and Administration of Assessments, including representative sampling, preparation and communication with schools, training and deployment of field staff, implementation and monitoring of the pilot and main assessments, secure handling of assessment materials, coding and scoring, data entry, and quality assurance;
  • Psychometric Analysis and Reporting, including IRT-based analysis, calibration and scaling, standard setting, preparation of national and school-level reports and system-level recommendations, dissemination of results, and measures supporting data protection, knowledge transfer, and sustainability of the national assessment system;
  • System-Level Training and Dissemination of Results, including capacity building for the IEQE and other relevant institutions, as well as training and support for education advisers, school principals, and teachers in the interpretation and use of national assessment results for policy development, school improvement, and teaching practice.

The Government of Mozambique (GoM), through the National Youth Institute (INJ) under the supervision of the Ministry of Youth and Sports (MJD), and with the support of the World Bank, is implementing the “East Africa Girls' Empowerment and Resilience” (EAGER) investment project. In Mozambique, the EAGER investment operation (2024 to 2029) is implemented jointly by the Ministry of Labor, Gender, and Social Action (MTGAS) and the MJD.

SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATIONS D’INTERET

 

Pays : Burundi

Nom du Projet : Projet pour l’Emploi et la Transformation Economique (PRETE)

Numéro de Prêt/Crédit/Don:  Don IDA N° E-2650-BI

N° du projet: P172988

 

Intitule de la mission : Spécialiste en Micro, Petites et Moyennes Entreprises (MPME) du PRETE

Numéro de référence (selon le Plan de Passation des marchés) : BI-ADB-571156-CS-INDV

La République du Burundi a obtenu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour couvrir le coût du Projet pour l’Emploi et la Transformation Economique (PRETE), et a l'intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce don pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat suivant : « Spécialiste en Micro, Petites et Moyennes Entreprises (MPME) du PRETE ».

Les services de consultants (« les services ») consistent à appuyer techniquement l’UGP du PRETE dans la préparation, la coordination, le suivi et la qualité de la mise en œuvre de la Composante 1 « Accès des MPME aux marchés et développement des chaînes de valeur ». Le/la Spécialiste en Micro, Petites et Moyennes Entreprises (MPME) du PRETE veillera à la cohérence et à la qualité technique des activités conduites au titre des sous-composantes 1.1, 1.2 et 1.3 et à leur contribution à l’atteinte des résultats du projet.

La durée des prestations s’étend jusqu’à la date de clôture du Projet (29/12/2028) à partir de la notification du contrat.

Les termes de référence détaillés (TdR) pour la mission peuvent être obtenus à l'adresse indiquée ci-dessous ou par mail.

L’Unité de gestion du PRETE invite maintenant les candidats éligibles (« Consultants individuels ») à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les Services. Les candidats intéressés doivent fournir toutes les informations nécessaires démontrant qu'ils possèdent les qualifications requises et l'expérience pertinente pour exécuter les services. Le Consultant devra répondre aux critères suivants :

  • Être titulaire au minimum d’un Master en sciences économiques, gestion, administration des affaires, entrepreneuriat, sciences du développement, sciences sociales ou dans une autre discipline pertinente ;
  • Avoir au moins cinq (5) années d’expérience professionnelle pertinente dans le développement, l’accompagnement ou l’appui aux Micro, Petites et Moyennes Entreprises (MPME), dont une expérience significative au Burundi ;
  • Justifier d’une expérience avérée dans la conception, la préparation, la coordination, la mise en œuvre et/ou le suivi de programmes en faveur des MPME, notamment dans les domaines de l’accès aux marchés, des chaînes de valeur, du développement des fournisseurs, de l’accompagnement entrepreneurial, du renforcement des capacités et de l’adoption des technologies ;
  • Avoir une expérience pratique en matière d’accès des MPME aux infrastructures productives, d’amélioration de la productivité et de la compétitivité, de certification et de qualité, de développement de partenariats et de mise en relation commerciale ;
  • Avoir une bonne connaissance de l’écosystème du secteur privé et des MPME au Burundi, notamment des institutions publiques, chambres de commerce, organisations professionnelles, institutions financières, entreprises principales, prestataires de services et structures d’appui aux entreprises ;
  • Posséder une bonne compréhension des principales contraintes auxquelles sont confrontées les MPME burundaises, notamment en matière d’accès aux marchés, d’intégration dans les chaînes de valeur, d’infrastructures productives, de financement, de technologies et transformation numérique, de compétences managériales et techniques, de normes et certification, ainsi que de résilience au changement climatique ;
  • Avoir une expérience de collaboration avec des institutions publiques, des organisations du secteur privé, des chambres de commerce, des associations professionnelles, des partenaires techniques et financiers et/ou des programmes de développement ;
  • Une expérience dans la préparation de PTBA, de termes de référence, de dossiers techniques et dans la collaboration avec des projets financés par la Banque mondiale ou d’autres partenaires au développement constitue un atout ;
  • Avoir une bonne capacité d’organisation du travail, de planification, d’analyse, de rédaction de rapports et de préparation de documents techniques ;
  • Être capable d’effectuer des missions sur le terrain et de travailler avec des équipes, partenaires et bénéficiaires dans différents contextes ;
  • Avoir une bonne maîtrise des logiciels informatiques standards, notamment Word, Excel, PowerPoint et des outils usuels de communication et de collaboration en ligne ;
  • Avoir une intégrité professionnelle, un sens élevé des responsabilités et de bonnes aptitudes à travailler en équipe ;
  • Avoir de bonnes aptitudes en communication écrite et orale et un bon sens des relations humaines ;
  • Avoir une bonne connaissance du français écrit et parlé et une bonne maîtrise de l’anglais.

L'attention des Consultants intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement FPI » de septembre 2023 (« Règlement »), énonçant la politique de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d'intérêts.

Un consultant sera sélectionné conformément à la méthode de Sélection des Consultants Individuels avec approche ouverte nationale, énoncée dans le Règlement de passation des marchés de la Banque mondiale pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le (FPI), Edition de septembre 2023 et conformément aux critères exigés par les termes de référence.

title: Provision of Consultancy Services for the Development of the Organization and Design of Museum and Cultural Spaces at the Dvin and Dashtadem Sites
project_name: Armenia Tourism and Regional Infrastructure Project
notice_text:
TRIP-CQS-02

                                                                                                                    TERMS OF REFERENCE

Provision of Consulting Services for the Planning and Design Development of the Dvin and Dashtadem Museum and Cultural Sites under the Implementation of TRIP-DP-01 and TRIP-DP-02 Subprojects in the Republic of Armenia

  1. BACKGROUND

The Tourism and Regional Infrastructure Program (TRIP) aims to promote Armenia’s tourism potential through targeted infrastructure and non-infrastructure investments in a number of regions. The Program will support seven out of the twenty identified tourism clusters, focusing on wine, wellness, adventure, cultural, educational, and ecotourism in the regions of Ararat, Vayots Dzor, Shirak, Tavush, and Syunik. Within the framework of the Program, access to the identified clusters will be improved, and infrastructure at tourism destinations will be developed. The Program also seeks to leverage Armenia’s natural resources and human potential by developing the entrepreneurial and professional skills of residents of neighboring communities, with the aim of maximizing employment opportunities. In addition, the TRIP Program is aligned with the World Bank’s approach to attracting private investment to these tourism clusters.

The infrastructure investment component of the TRIP Program includes the construction of new public buildings, including museum buildings; the restoration and preservation of historical and cultural monuments; the revitalization of the urban environment of historic towns and villages, including the restoration of building façades, public spaces, museums, and roads; as well as the improvement of cultural and natural heritage sites, including ensuring their accessibility and appropriate presentation.

Under the World Bank’s Local Economy and Infrastructure Development (LEID) Project, which preceded the Tourism and Regional Infrastructure (TRIP) Program, designs for the museum buildings at the Dvin archaeological site and Dashtadem Fortress were developed and approved in 2024. Based on these designs, construction works will be implemented under the TRIP Program.

Under the TRIP Program, in parallel with the work of the museum specialist, the design documentation will be updated, the cost estimate will be recalculated based on current prices, and the accompanying documentation will be updated, including the Architectural Planning Assignment (APA), technical specifications, expert examination conclusions, approvals, and other relevant documents. The revision of the design will be carried out through the conclusion of a direct contract with the original design author.

At present, within the framework of the TRIP Program, it is necessary to develop conceptual approaches for the organization of the museum environment and exhibitions for the museums at the Dvin and Dashtadem archaeological sites, including exhibition design, taking into consideration their respective missions, visions, and objectives.

 

  1. OBJECTIVE OF THE ASSIGNMENT

Objective of the Assignment

The objective of the assignment is to:

  • Dvin: Present the archaeological museum of Dvin and the preserved monuments of the archaeological site of the “Capital of Dvin” to tourists by creating a culturally rich and, at the same time, scientific and educational environment that is historically grounded while incorporating modern amenities and design, archaeological exhibits, and historical reconstructions.
    Proposed museum type: Archaeological Museum.
  • Dashtadem: Determine the type and content of the Dashtadem Museum; develop and collect exhibits; plan interactive activities and festivals; recreate historical events using the entire area of the large fortress; and incorporate all structures of the restored fortress into programs featuring reenactments of historical episodes and military-sport games.
    Proposed museum type: Military-Historical Museum, though a broader historical scope could also be suggested (subject to further discussion).

Expected Results of the Assignment

The expected result of the assignment is the establishment of operational archaeological and military-historical museums at Dvin and Dashtadem, respectively, featuring:

  • Exhibitions developed on a sound scientific basis;
  • Modern lighting and design;
  • Information delivered through multimedia tools;
  • A management system compliant with modern museum standards, including digitized databases and appropriate conditions for the preservation, conservation/restoration, and display of exhibits;
  • Increased tourist visitation and increased tourism-generated revenues.

 

  1. SCOPE OF SERVICES

The scope of consulting services is divided into three phases:

Phase 1. Preliminary Study, Collection Assessment and Documentation, and Development of the Exhibition Concept and Layout Plans

This phase shall include a preliminary study of the sites and museums, assessment and documentation of the existing collections, and development of the conceptual approach to the organization of the exhibitions and the relevant layout plans.

Phase 2. Development of Museum Content, Exhibition Planning, and Development of Exhibition Design and Lighting Schemes

This phase shall include the development of the museums’ content, exhibition planning, and the development of exhibition design and lighting schemes for both interior and exterior spaces, in accordance with the requirements applicable to the “Design Developement” stage.

Phase 3. Integration of the Approved Solutions into the Museum Design Documentation, Capacity Building, Support for the Development of Management Policies, and Final Reporting

This phase shall include:

  • Integration of the solutions approved under Phase 2 into the design documentation of the museums;
  • Capacity building for museum staff;
  • Support for the development of museum management policies; and
  • Preparation and submission of the final report.

The interim and final deliverables shall be submitted to the Armenian Territorial Development Fund (ATDF) (the Client) for review and comments.

Key Stakeholders

The key stakeholders of the assignment are:

  • The Ministry of Economy of the Republic of Armenia, Tourism Committee (MoE Tourism Committee);
  • The Ministry of Education, Science, Culture and Sports of the Republic of Armenia (MoESCS);
  • The World Bank;
  • The “Service for the Protection of Historical Environment and Cultural Museum-Reservations” State Non-Commercial Organization; and
  • Relevant local self-government and state administration bodies.

 

PHASE 1. PRELIMINARY STUDY, COLLECTION ASSESSMENT AND DOCUMENTATION, AND DEVELOPMENT OF THE EXHIBITION CONCEPT AND LAYOUT PLANS

Task 1. Preliminary Study

  • Study the key objectives and priorities of the Program, as well as the principles governing the organization and development of similar museums.
  • Review the existing collections and exhibits; review and update the collection inventory; and assess the physical condition of the collections, the level of documentation, the potential for expanding the exhibitions, and opportunities for the application of modern technologies and best practices.
  • Update or create object records/passports for the collection items in the Collection Management System (CMS) or other appropriate information platforms.
  • Review the design documentation for the Dvin and Dashtadem museums and assess all spaces suitable for exhibition purposes.
  • Conduct inception meetings with the museum (and archaeological site) management and relevant departments to discuss existing challenges and perspectives, with the participation of all relevant stakeholders. The Client (ATDF) shall be notified in advance of the scheduled meetings.
  • Prepare and submit to the Client a brief report summarizing the work carried out, meetings held, and recommendations and proposals received from stakeholders.

 

Task 2. Collection Assessment and Documentation

For Dvin:

  • Classify the exhibits and archaeological finds into two lists: items intended for display and items to be placed in storage for further study and/or conservation/restoration.
  • For the items intended for display, identify their proposed display locations, such as exhibition halls, entrance/lobby areas, outdoor platforms, excavated pits protected by glass covers or shelters, and other appropriate locations.
  • Assess the informational signage and other small-scale architectural elements included in the design, and provide recommendations on whether they should be retained or modified.
  • Prepare preliminary classified lists of exhibits and archaeological finds according to their proposed display locations (e.g., exhibition hall, entrance/lobby, outdoor areas, archaeological site recreation/rest area, etc.).

 

For Dashtadem:

  • Identify, collect information on, and inventory all potential exhibits and archaeological finds, including their current locations and the organizations holding them. Classify them into two lists: items intended for display and items to be placed in storage for further study and/or conservation/restoration, indicating the current location of each exhibit and the arrangements made for obtaining/accessing it.
  • Propose a list of exhibits to be reconstructed and/or reproduced, together with sketches or photographs of relevant examples.
  • Assess the informational signage and other small-scale architectural elements included in the design, and provide recommendations on whether they should be retained or modified.
  • Prepare preliminary classified lists of exhibits and archaeological finds according to their proposed display locations (e.g., exhibition hall, entrance/lobby, outdoor areas, archaeological site recreation/rest area, etc.).

Task 3. Development of the Exhibition Concept and Layout Plans

For Dvin and Dashtadem:

  • Develop the exhibition concept, including proposed display locations, visitor circulation routes, descriptions, justification of the selected exhibition schemes, principles for organizing the interior spaces, the proposed design and lighting style, the placement of information panels and exhibit labels, and other relevant elements.

Consolidated Deliverables for Tasks 1–3

The findings and outputs of Tasks 1–3 shall be consolidated into two comprehensive reports, one for Dvin and one for Dashtadem, with the following structure:

  • Summary description of the work carried out;
  • Museum organization concept, exhibition and lighting schemes, and classified list of exhibits;

PHASE 2. DEVELOPMENT OF MUSEUM CONTENT, EXHIBITION PLANNING, AND DEVELOPMENT OF EXHIBITION DESIGN AND LIGHTING SCHEMES FOR INTERIOR AND EXTERIOR SPACES

 

!!! The activities under Phase 2 shall be developed in accordance with the solutions approved under Phase 1.

!!! Any new concept, idea, or solution shall be agreed with the Client in advance.

!!! The outputs shall be developed as separate packages for Dvin and Dashtadem.

Task 1. Development of Museum Content and Exhibition Planning

  • Define the overall exhibition concept, the key interpretation themes, and the expected learning outcomes for visitors, ensuring their alignment with the cultural and historical significance of the archaeological site.
  • Prepare curatorial notes and research dossiers for significant exhibits. At the same time, define the key interpretation themes and sub-themes that will connect the exhibits to meaningful narratives and visitor experiences.
  • Develop the exhibition narrative structure, storylines, and educational content.
  • Develop the textual content of the exhibition, including labels, information panels, guides, and catalogues.
  • Develop all informational materials, exhibit labels, and other textual materials in Armenian and English, with the Armenian and English texts presented together on the same exhibit labels, posters, and other information panels.
  • Integrate the descriptive content of the exhibition into audio and video systems in order to enhance visitors’ understanding of and overall experience of the exhibition.

Task 2. Development of Exhibition Design and Lighting Schemes for Interior and Exterior Spaces

  • Develop a master plan incorporating the archaeological site, historical structures, and the museum, including:
    • The visitor routes approved under Phase 1, indicating the entrance, exit, and visitor stops, including historical structures and cultural sites; selected outdoor exhibits; posters and information signage; viewing platforms; pavilions; the museum’s main exhibition halls; temporary exhibition spaces; outdoor pavilions and recreation areas; cafés; restrooms; excavated areas; parking areas; and other relevant facilities;
    • A tourist route map developed on the basis of the master plan, with the potential for subsequent publication and use as a tourist map.
  • Develop layout plans and/or wall elevations for the placement of exhibits in the main exhibition hall and other areas, including entrance/lobby areas, passageways, corridors, and outdoor platforms, covering:
    • The location of each exhibit, exhibit identification number, exhibit name, photograph, and accompanying label text in Armenian and English;
    • Pedestals, supports, tables, display cases, shelving, and exhibit mounting/installation schemes;
    • Modular solutions enabling exhibits to be periodically replaced, temporary exhibitions to be organized, and the museum exhibition to be updated in the future.
  • Develop the detailed design of furniture and display equipment for all spaces included in the visitor routes, including exhibit pedestals, supports, display cases, shelves, etc., in accordance with the requirements of the “Design develoment” stage and with sufficient detail to enable a furniture manufacturer to prepare detailed shop drawings and manufacture the items based on the design.
  • Develop the exhibition lighting scheme and lighting scenarios, including specifications for lighting fixtures.
  • Develop audio-visual system schemes and equipment specifications.
  • Provide recommendations regarding other engineering systems, where applicable.
  • Provide a list of potential companies capable of manufacturing the proposed furniture and display equipment, together with their submitted price quotations, from at least three companies.

 

!!! Ensure that all exhibition supports, display cases, information panels, lighting systems, and digital/interactive elements comply with current international best practices in museology, accessibility, and preventive conservation of exhibits.

Additional Requirements for Dashtadem

  • Develop sketches and detailed descriptions of exhibits to be reproduced and/or reconstructed, including weapons, military equipment and clothing, tools, means of transportation, and other relevant items, based on the analysis of historical sources and/or archaeological finds.
  • Develop sketches of mannequins representing military personnel from different historical periods, including detailed designs and specifications of the respective uniforms /if a broader historical scope is accepted for Dashtadem, the sketches may also include examples from secular life/.
  • For the three outdoor pavilions representing the workshops of a medieval blacksmith, leatherworker, and carpenter, provide descriptions of the furnishings and equipment, illustrative sketches, dimensions, materials of manufacture, and other details sufficient to enable the procurement or fabrication of the required furnishings and equipment.

 

Duration and Timeline of Phase 2

Duration: 120 calendar days.

Implementation period: 180 calendar days from the day following the date of signing of the Contract, including the process of review, comments, and approval of the reports.

Deliverables for Phase 2

Package 1 – Dvin

The package shall include:

  • Master plan, visitor route, and design and content of information panels;
  • Tourist route map, ready for printing;
  • Exhibition layout plan, list of exhibits, and descriptions;
  • Lighting scheme, lighting scenarios, and specifications;
  • Audio-visual system schemes and equipment specifications;
  • Other recommendations.

Package 2 – Dashtadem

The package shall include:

  • Master plan, visitor route, and design and content of information panels;
  • Tourist route map, ready for printing;
  • Exhibition layout plan, list of exhibits, and descriptions;
  • Sketches of exhibits to be reproduced and reconstructed, descriptions of materials and methods of production, historical clothing and equipment patterns/templates, and mannequin sketches;
  • Sketches of the furnishings and equipment for the medieval blacksmith, leatherworker, and carpenter workshops, including fabrication instructions and other relevant details;
  • Lighting scheme, lighting scenarios, and specifications;
  • Audio-visual system schemes and equipment specifications;
  • Other recommendations.

Indicators of Achievement for Phase 2

  • Approval by the Client of both packages:
    • Package 1 – Dvin; and
    • Package 2 – Dashtadem.

 

PHASE 3. INTEGRATION OF APPROVED SOLUTIONS INTO THE MUSEUM DESIGN DOCUMENTATION, MUSEUM STAFF CAPACITY BUILDING AND SUPPORT FOR POLICY DEVELOPMENT, AND SUBMISSION OF THE FINAL REPORT

Task 1. Integration of the Solutions Approved under Phase 2 into the Museum Design Documentation

  • Develop Design Assignment No. 1, containing clear instructions regarding the changes, additions, and further developments to be incorporated into the design and cost-estimate documentation of the Dvin and Dashtadem museums. The assignment shall be substantiated by the schemes, specifications, and instructions approved under Phase 2.
  • Develop Design Assignment No. 2, containing clear requirements to be included in procurement requests for the acquisition and/or fabrication of furniture and reconstructed/reproduced exhibits. The assignment shall be substantiated by the design developed and approved under Phase 2, including sketches, schemes, specifications, quantities, and other relevant instructions.

Task 2. Museum Staff Capacity Building and Support for Policy Development

  • Organize training sessions and/or workshops for museum staff (at this stage, the staff of the “Service for the Protection of Historical Environment and Cultural Museum-Reservations” SNCO) on the following topics:
    • Best practices in exhibition curatorial work;
    • Collection registration and documentation;
    • Exhibition development and organization;
    • Improvement of institutional activities and processes, as applicable, including:
      • Collection Management Policy;
      • Collection Acquisition and Deaccession Policy;
      • Conservation and Preventive Care Policy;
      • Exhibition and Interpretation Policy;
      • Object Loan and Reproduction Policy;
      • Digitization and Information Access Policy.

Task 3. Submission of the Final Report

  • Prepare and submit the Final Report on the Consulting Services, which shall include:
    • A summary description of the work carried out;
    • The final, revised and proofread packages of all deliverables specified for all phases, submitted in electronic format and four (4) hard copies;
    • Minutes/proceedings of meetings, consultations, discussions, and training sessions conducted, including lists of participants;
    • Strategic recommendations aimed at ensuring the sustainability of the museum’s operations and supporting the further development of its institutional capacities.

 

Duration and Timeline of Phase 3

Duration: 40 calendar days.

Implementation period: 220 calendar days from the day following the date of signing of the Contract, including the process of review, comments, and approval of the reports.

Deliverables for Phase 3

  • Design Assignment No. 1 and Design Assignment No. 2 – Dvin;
  • Design Assignment No. 1 and Design Assignment No. 2 – Dashtadem;
  • Report on the training sessions conducted and support provided, signed by the head of the organization that received the training and/or support.

Indicators of Achievement for Phase 3

  • Approval by the Client of the submitted Design Assignments and the Report.

 

  1. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS, IMPLEMENTATION MECHANISMS AND ALLOCATION OF RESPONSIBILITIES
    1.  Language of Development
  • The deliverables envisaged under Phases 1–3 shall be prepared and submitted in Armenian.
  • Museum exhibit labels, texts for information panels, information delivered through audio-visual media, and other visitor guidance and interpretive textual materials shall be developed bilingually, in Armenian and English.
  • Training sessions and support shall be provided in Armenian, or with Armenian interpretation provided.
    1. Submission Formats and Supporting Materials

Each deliverable shall be submitted in both editable and non-editable formats and shall include:

  • Textual materials: MS Word and PDF;
  • Graphic materials: AutoCAD (or other appropriate graphic design software) and PDF;
  • Calculations, lists, specifications, and other tables: Excel, Word, and PDF formats.
    1. Criteria for Review and Acceptance of Submitted Work

Each deliverable shall be considered acceptable if it:

  • Fully complies with the scope of the assignment;
  • Consistently meets the required content, structure, and level of detail;
  • Is consistent with previously approved deliverables; and
  • Incorporates revisions made based on comments received from the Client and relevant stakeholders.
    1. Review and Approval Sequence

All deliverables shall be submitted and reviewed according to the following sequence:

  1. Initial submission by the Consultant to the Client (ATDF);
  2. Coordination with the MoE Tourism Committee and relevant stakeholders, including the MoESCS, World Bank, and other relevant authorities;
  3. Consolidated comments communicated to the Consultant through the ATDF;
  4. Submission by the Consultant of a revised version incorporating all comments, including the relevant revisions and/or clarifications;
  5. Obtaining “no objection” confirmation from the MoE Tourism Committee, MoESCS, World Bank, and other relevant authorities regarding the revised materials;
  6. Final approval by the Tourism Committee and acceptance by the ATDF.
    1. Review Periods
  • Each review stage shall not exceed three (3) weeks from the date of submission.
  • The Consultant shall be provided with one to two (1–2) weeks to incorporate comments and submit the revised version.
  • The duration of the review process, number of review iterations, and approval procedure shall be agreed upon during the inception stage.
    1. Scope of the Consultant’s Activities and Responsibilities

The Consultant shall be responsible for:

  • Collecting and studying historical data related to the two cultural sites; conducting site visits and field assessments; and collecting, studying, classifying, and supplementing information on exhibits related to the sites;
  • Cooperating with specialists in the cultural, museum, and archaeological fields; determining the types of the Dvin and Dashtadem museums (archaeological, historical, thematic, etc.) and agreeing the proposed museum types with the Client;
  • Studying and analyzing baseline data, existing materials, and approved design documentation;
  • Preparing conceptual/sketch proposals for the content, organization, and design of the exhibitions and agreeing them with the Client;
  • Developing and agreeing with the Client the design of the furnishing of the museum buildings, including exhibit pedestals, niches, supports, exhibition hall partitions, exhibits displayed in entrance/lobby areas, posters, signage, and other related elements;
  • Developing the lighting system and lighting scenarios for exhibition halls and other public spaces, and providing specifications for lighting fixtures;
  • Designing audio-visual systems for the museums and preparing audio and video guides;
  • Within the scope of its assignment, the museum specialist may propose changes to the functional designation of certain rooms, subject to agreement with the Client (e.g., auditorium/lecture hall, temporary exhibition hall, café, workshop/studio for children, etc.);
  • Organizing training sessions and providing support to museum staff;
  • Cooperating with the design organization under the coordination of the Client.

The Consultant shall be responsible for the timely delivery of high-quality outputs, as well as for effective communication and coordination of activities with the Client and the Program stakeholders.

The Consultant shall not be responsible for the physical collection or acquisition of archaeological objects and other exhibits. However, the Consultant shall provide recommendations regarding their selection, acquisition, scholarly interpretation, and display.

The Consultant shall prepare an Exhibit Identification and Acquisition Plan, specifying:

  • Proposed exhibits and collections;
  • Locations of the exhibits, potential acquisition opportunities, and preliminary arrangements;
  • Exhibits to be provided by archaeological expeditions, museums, state institutions, or private collections;
  • Exhibits requiring reproduction, reconstruction, illustration, modeling, or creation of a digital version;
  • Recommendations regarding the development of replicas, scale models, audiovisual materials, and interactive interpretation tools.

The Consultant’s recommendations shall not require changes to the architectural and/or structural solutions included in the Museum designs. Where recommendations concerning finishes or interior treatments are made, they shall be coordinated with the design author and the Client.

At the Client’s request, the Consultant shall prepare reports/presentations on visitor routes, exhibition schemes, and furniture/display design. The Consultant shall be prepared, under the coordination of the Client, to discuss the proposed solutions with the Design Team, stakeholders, and community representatives.

The Consultant shall participate in working meetings organized by the Client to ensure the accuracy, completeness, and integration of the exhibition content and the interconnection of its various components.

The Consultant shall independently bear all costs associated with the provision of the consulting services, including:

  • Transportation costs;
  • Office and administrative expenses;
  • Costs related to organizing meetings;
  • Costs of interpretation and translation services;
  • Costs of printing and reproduction of documents.
    1.   Client Responsibilities and Scope of Activities

The Client shall ensure coordination among the Museum Specialist, the Designer, and all relevant stakeholders.

The Client shall coordinate the deliverables submitted for each phase with the MoESCS, MoE Tourism Committee, World Bank, and, as necessary, other relevant stakeholders. Upon obtaining the required coordination and approval from the MoE Tourism Committee, the Client shall accept the respective deliverable.

The deliverables of each phase shall be approved before proceeding to the activities of the subsequent phase. The approval timelines shall be agreed upon among the relevant stakeholders; however, as a general principle, they shall not exceed ten (10) working days.

Following the Client’s acceptance of proposals submitted by the Museum Specialist’s team that involve modifications to the lighting, audio-visual, and/or other engineering systems, such proposals shall be forwarded to the design authoring organization with instructions to incorporate them into the working design documentation and cost estimate.

The production of furniture, exhibit pedestals, and other soft elements shall be procured by the Client through a separate procurement process. The design proposals, sketches, and three-dimensional visualizations developed by the Museum Specialist shall contain sufficient information to enable the furniture manufacturer to prepare detailed shop drawings and manufacture the furniture and related elements.

    1. Intellectual Property Requirements

The Consultant shall be the author of the work prepared under this Terms of Reference, and the work shall constitute the Consultant’s intellectual property.

The Client shall be the owner of the accepted work and may use it at its discretion, in whole or in part. In the event that substantial modifications become necessary during the implementation period, the Client shall discuss such modifications with the Consultant.

The Client undertakes not to use the outputs of the work for other museums and/or buildings or structures of a different nature.

The Consultant shall not have the right to disseminate, publish, include in lectures, or present on other public platforms any interim outputs of the work until the work has been fully completed and formally accepted by the Client.

Any disputes not regulated under this section shall be resolved in accordance with the procedure established by the legislation of the Republic of Armenia.

 

  1. DATA, DOCUMENTS AND SUPPORT TO BE PROVIDED BY THE CLIENT

The Client shall provide the Consultant with the design documentation for the two museums, the lists of exhibits intended for display and storage at the Dvin Museum, and reports on archaeological excavations carried out at the Dashtadem Fortress site at different times.

The documents to be provided by the Client include:

  • Design and cost-estimate documentation package for the “Improvement of the Dvin Archaeological Site and Adjacent Area and Provision of Tourism Infrastructure” project

Ref No.:                               SO-MPWRH-568985-CS-CQS

1. The Federal Government of Somalia has received financing from the World Bank (International Development Association) towards the cost of the Somalia Infrastructure Development for Access and Jobs, Phase 1 (P513127) – the first phase of a Multiphase Programmatic Approach (MPA) – and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

2. The consulting services (“the Services”) comprise the preparation of a complete, construction-ready detailed design package (architectural, structural, civil, and mechanical/electrical/plumbing) and a World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF)-compliant set of environmental and social instruments (including an Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA), an Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP), and any resettlement, labor, stakeholder engagement, and health-and-safety instruments triggered by the proposed works) for a new MoPWRH headquarters building, on an identified plot of approximately 120 m x 50 m (approximately 6,000 m²) in the Shangani District, Mogadishu. The assignment also includes preparation of a detailed cost estimate, Bill of Quantities (BoQ), and complete tender/bidding documents suitable for competitive procurement of construction works under a future MPA phase. The Consultant will undertake all the specific tasks detailed in the Terms of Reference. The duration of the assignment is six (6) months, and the estimated professional staff-months is 36.

3. The Detailed Terms of Reference for this assignment, with the scope of the assignment, can be found on the Ministry of Public Works, Reconstruction and Housing’s website: www.mpwr.gov.so, or it can be provided upon submission of the application by e-mail to the e-mail address provided below.

4. The Ministry of Public Works, Reconstruction and Housing of the Federal Government of Somalia (“Client”) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The shortlisting criteria are as follows:

  • Core business and years in business: The firm shall be registered/incorporated as a consulting firm with core business in any of the following areas: (i) Architectural and Building Engineering Design Services; (ii) Civil/Structural Engineering Consulting Services; (iii) Environmental and Social Consulting Services; or (iv) Urban and Infrastructure Planning Services, for a period of at least ten (10) years.
  • Relevant experience: The firm shall demonstrate experience in: (i) detailed design (architectural, structural, and mechanical/electrical/plumbing) of multi-story public or institutional buildings; and (ii) preparation of environmental and social safeguards instruments under the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) or an equivalent multilateral development bank (MDB) safeguards system (such as the former OP/BP 4.01 or IFC Performance Standards); as well as experience in any two of the following: (i) geotechnical investigation and structural design in seismic and/or coastal environments; (ii) cost estimation, Bill of Quantities preparation, and tender/bidding documentation for public works procured under World Bank or comparable MDB procurement procedures; (iii) stakeholder engagement and consultation for infrastructure or building projects; and (iv) work in fragile and conflict-affected settings (FCV), particularly in Somalia or comparable Horn of Africa/East Africa contexts. Additionally, the firm should demonstrate successful execution and completion of at least two (2) assignments of a similar nature and in a similar operating environment in the last ten (10) years. Details of similar assignments – name and address of the client, scope, value, and period – should be included in the Expression of Interest (EOI).
  • Technical and managerial capability of the firm: The firm(s) shall demonstrate as having the requisite technical capability, which shall entail a description of relevant personnel, equipment, software, etc., and managerial capacity to undertake the assignment. The maximum page limit for the EOI, including any annexes, is 20 pages. This limit applies for single entities as well as firms in associations.

5. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, First Published July 2016 and Revised in September 2023 (5th Edition) (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

7. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Selection based on Consultants’ Qualifications (CQS) method set out in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers.

8. Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Mogadishu time (excluding public holidays).

1. The Federal Government of Somalia (FGS) (hereinafter called “Recipient”) has received financing from the World Bank through the International Development Association (IDA) (hereinafter called “Grant”) toward the cost of the Somalia Infrastructure Development for Access and Jobs, Phase 1 (Stairs2Jobs MPA). The Ministry of Public Works, Reconstruction and Housing (MoPWRH), through its Project Implementation Unit (MoPWRH-PIU), intends to apply a portion of the proceeds to finance the position of a Health and Safety Expert.

2. The objective of the assignment is to support the MoPWRH-PIU in improving construction zone safety and promoting safe working practices across all active urban drainage and road corridor work sites under the project, including the priority trunk drainage works for Catchment Outfall O16 in Mogadishu and the Haleya–Ina Guha Economic Corridor. The Expert will manage occupational health and safety (OHS) risks, support contractors to operationalize site-specific health and safety plans, build E&S capacity within the Ministry, and ensure that all works comply with national regulations, the World Bank Environmental and Social Standards (particularly ESS2 and ESS4) and the approved project E&S instruments.

3. The Health and Safety Expert will, among other tasks: ensure that OHS requirements of the ESIA/ESMP are incorporated into bidding documents, contract specifications and Bills of Quantities (including costed provisions for PPE and site safety measures); monitor construction sites and carry out regular and unannounced safety inspections, recommending corrective actions; deliver safety training, site orientations and toolbox talks for contractors, workers and MoPWRH staff; maintain records of near-misses, injuries and incidents and lead incident investigations; support the Grievance Redress Mechanism in handling safety-related grievances; and prepare regular OHS compliance, inspection and training reports.

4. Duration: This is a full-time position under a time-based contract. The contract is expected to run for a period of twelve (12) calendar months, with frequent field deployments to active project sites. Extension of the contract will be subject to the need and satisfactory performance of the consultant.

5. Selection Criteria: The selection shall be based on the qualifications, experience and skills of the candidate, followed by an interview. The qualifications, experience and skills should include: a Bachelor’s degree in Occupational Health and Safety, Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Construction Management, Public Health or a related discipline; an internationally recognized OHS certification such as NEBOSH (International General Certificate, Construction Certificate or Diploma), IOSH, CSP, CMIOSH or equivalent; a minimum of 7–10 years of progressively responsible OHS experience, including at least 5 years of direct experience supporting major infrastructure projects (roads, drainage, airports, ports, water, energy or other heavy civil works); demonstrated experience in contractor OHS management, incident investigation, root-cause analysis, OHS audits and construction safety management systems; familiarity with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework, particularly ESS2 and ESS4; experience working in fragile and conflict-affected environments; professional fluency in written and spoken Somali and English; and the readiness to undertake frequent, extended field deployments to project sites.

6. MoPWRH now invites eligible Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the above-mentioned services. Interested consultants must provide information indicating that they are qualified to perform the Services and furnish the Curriculum Vitae (CV) in the prescribed form that will be provided with the TOR upon submission of application (by e-mail at the address given below).

The subject line of the e-mail should clearly indicate: SO-MPWRH-570560-CS-INDV: HEALTH AND SAFETY EXPERT.

Place of assignment:                   Mogadishu, Somalia

Submission Date:                         October 19, 2026, 2.00pm (local time, Mogadishu, Somalia)

The Federal Republic of Somalia has received a grant from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank toward the cost of the Regional Digital Integration Project (EA-RDIP), and the Ministry of Communications and Technology intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“Services”) is required to be undertaken as an external consultant firm supporting the client, Ministry of Communications and Technology (MoCT), FGS to carry out the implementation of “Government Data Governance, Interoperability Standards and Digital Service Risk Framework”. The assignment aims to establish a coherent, standardized and implementable government-wide foundation for data governance, interoperability, data exchange, reference and master data management, and digital service risk management across the Federal Government of Somalia. This includes developing government-wide standards for open data, metadata, APIs, registry data and digital service design; a Master Data Management Governance Framework and Register of Authoritative Sources; a Government Common Data Model; data quality, data-sharing and data classification frameworks; a Digital Service Risk-Profile Framework; and a sequenced implementation roadmap. The consultant firm will undertake all the specific required tasks detailed out in the Terms of Reference (ToR). The consultant service is expected to be conducted and reports delivered in approximately sixteen (16) weeks from contract effectiveness.

TERMS OF REFERENCE

CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL SELECTION

TERMS OF REFERENCE FOR INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT

PART I: 

Position

Operations Manager

Category of Consultancy

Local (Level 5)

Contract Type

Time-based Individual Consultant

Hiring Entity

TRHDP Project Office

Location

Honiara, Solomon Islands

Duration

2 years

Start date

As soon as possible upon agreement

 

 

Tina River Hydropower Development Project              

Project Details

Strategic Context

The Tina River Hydropower Project is the first large-scale infrastructure to be developed under a public-private partnership arrangement and the first utility-scale renewable energy project for the Solomon Islands expected to deliver benefits such as more affordable electricity and improved accessibility to cleaner, more reliable energy sources for community now and in the future.

 

The Tina River Hydropower Project consists of (i) 15-megawatt hydropower facility located on the Tina River southeast of Honiara, comprising: a dam, headrace tunnel and a powerhouse about 3km downstream of the dam; (ii) access road to facilitate the construction and operation of the hydropower facility; and (iii) transmission lines - two parallel (on separate poles) single circuit transmission lines connecting the powerhouse to the existing Lungga Power Station. Further project details are included in Annex A.

 

The Tina Hydro Project Office under the Ministry of Mines, Energy and Rural Electrification is responsible for the coordination of the project activities to ensure Tina Hydropower Limited as implementing entity responsible for the hydropower facility and access road and Solomon Power as Offtaker under the Power Purchase Agreement fulfil their obligations under the project agreements. The Project Office has a fundamental advisory role to Solomon Islands Government, ensuring that the interests of the government are protected in line with the project agreements. The Project Office is responsible for monitoring and supporting the implementation of the social and environmental safeguard arrangements, the Gender Action Plan and Community Development Plan, and maintaining the Dam Safety Advisory Panel (DSAP) and the Lender’s Technical Advisor (LTA) including the independent social and environmental monitoring agent. The Project Office also supports entities participating in the implementation arrangements agreed under the land acquisition process, the communities in utilizing their share of project benefits for community development, and the tribes which would be interested and committed to the establishment of a protected area in the upper catchment.

 

The Operations Manager of the Project Office is expected to enhance leadership within the Project Office to efficiently support project implementation in the best interests of the Solomon Islands Government.

Contract Details

Details

Objective

The Operations Manager shall be based in Honiara, Solomon Islands, providing support to the Project Manager (PM) in managing the Tina River Hydropower Project Office.

Duration 

The position is for a period of 2 years with expected opportunity to renew subject to satisfactory performance evaluation rating by the PM annually.

Reporting

The Operations Manager will report to the PM. The Operations Manager will shadow the PM to learn the various aspects of the Project including the following:

  • All the 4 components of the Project
  • The Stakeholders
  • Implementation
  • Flow of funds
  • Agreements including EPC contract
  • The Financial Model
  • Additional financing
  • Technical aspects of the dam, tunnel and powerhouse
  • Pending work at the site
  • Up to date Disbursements
  • Future disbursements
  • Pending design issues
  • Role of LTA and DSAP
  • Meetings
  • SharePoint structure
  • Procurement through STEP
  • Status of contracts of the Consultants
  • Performance Management
  • World Bank and other CFP Missions, aide memoir

The Operations Manager will hold briefing meetings with the PM monthly or as otherwise agreed in writing with the PM.

 

The Operations Manager, under the guidance of the PM and Deputy Project Manager, will provide project implementation progress updates to the Project Steering Committee (PSC) at the quarterly PSC meetings or as required by the Chairperson of the PSC.

The Operations Manager will liaise and work very closely with the CBSP 2 Project Manager, the Deputy Project Manager and the Environmental and Social Safeguards Manager such that he/she develops a very good understanding of the finances, procurement, administrative, communications & media, grievance redress mechanism, gender action plan, biodiversity management plan, safeguards, health and safety, Tina Core Land Company (TCLC), Cooperatives, Land, Influx,  all 4 components of the Community Benefits Sharing Project 2 (CBSP2)

The Operations Manager will shadow the Project Manager; however, it is expected that he/she to learn about the project he/she will actively be involved in the deliverables listed on page 6. The Operations Manager will conduct and chair meetings, preparing the agenda and minutes of the meetings.

 

The Operations Manager will act in the role of the Project Manager during periods of absence of the PM from Honiara. During this period the Operations Manager will be solely responsible for the running of the Project Office. The delegations include: authority to endorse and sign purchase vouchers, review and approve timesheets for the ESSM, the Financial & Commercial Advisor (FCA), review and approve invoices from LTA, DSAP members, Ashurst, the FCA, the ESSM; review and approve agenda for the Project Steering Committee meetings, CFP missions, review and approve imprest requests, review/endorse memos from DSAP, correspond with THL on pending matters, conduct and chair progress meetings, chair meetings with ADB, WB, MMERE, MOFT and respond to emails.

 

The Project Office organization chart is included in Annex B.

 

 

DETAILED POSITION DESCRIPTION

           

The Operations Manager will support the PM, the Environmental and Social Safeguards Manager, the Deputy Project Manager and the CBSP 2 Project Manager for ensuring the effective and efficient management of the Project Office by:

 

  1. Implementing the project activities under the Project Office’s responsibility, including monitoring and supporting the implementation of the social and environmental safeguard arrangements, the Gender Action Plan and Community Development Plan.

 

  1. Supporting the entities participating in the implementation arrangements agreed under the land acquisition process (Tina Core Land Company and the five core landowning tribes’ co-operatives), the communities in utilizing their share of project benefits for community development through the CBSP project, and the tribes which would be interested and committed to the establishment of a protected area in the upper catchment.

 

  1. Monitoring the project activities of Tina Hydropower Limited as implementing entity responsible for the hydropower facility and access road and Solomon Power as Offtaker under the Power Purchase Agreement to ensure they fulfil their obligations under the project agreements.

 

  1. Monitoring Solomon Islands Government commitments to ensure it is meeting and maintaining its obligations as required by the project agreements.

 

The Operations Manager’s detailed project description is set out as follows.

 

General Responsibilities & Objectives

 

  • Overall in-depth understanding of the relevant documents/agreements including:
    • Project Documents including Power Purchase Agreement (PPA), Implementation Agreement (IA). Government Guarantee Agreement (GGA), the Land Lease Agreement and the Side Letter Agreement.

 

    • Financing agreements and project agreements of all Concessional Financing Partners (CFPs), the Facilities Agreement, and various security agreements and documents.

 

    • Safeguards documents including Environmental Social Impact Assessment (ESIA), Land Acquisition and Livelihood Restoration Plan (LALRP), Gender Action Plan (GAP), Community Development Plan (CDP); and implementation of the Construction Environment and Social Management Plans (CESMP).

 

    • Project Operations Manuals (POMs) and any other relevant documents.

 

  • Implement the project management system including suitable office administration for the Project Office, including appropriate document and records storage systems (SharePoint), communication, procurement, risk, meeting and administration management, ensure project management procedures and systems are accessible to all staff and consultants as relevant, and in consultation with the Deputy Project Manager, ESSM , train staff and consultants as relevant on the use of project management procedures and systems.

 

  • Assist the PM in the implementation of effective internal and external communication protocols as part of the overall project management procedures and systems.

 

  • Assist the PM in leading the coordination and collaboration of the key project stakeholders to ensure timely project implementation to resolve any major implementation hindrances efficiently and effectively.

 

  • Assist the PM to maintain an overview of the TCLC, and associated tribal cooperatives, and benefit share arrangements with a view to ensure that they are functioning according to the Land Lease Agreement and the Implementation Agreement.

 

Project Office Staff and Consultants

 

  • Assist the PM to oversee and manage the Project Office staff plan to ensure the Project Office is appropriately resourced to fulfil its mandate and implementation of the key project activities under its responsibility effectively and efficiently in accordance with the project agreements.

 

  • Work very closely with the Deputy Project Manager, Environmental and Social Safeguards manager to deliver in accordance with their terms of reference.

 

  • Review of Project Office staff and consultant performance in accordance with their contract terms and deliverables. Performance review will be coordinated in consultation with the Deputy Project Manager and Environmental and Social Safeguards Manager. Performance review will be on a six-monthly basis or as otherwise agreed in writing with the PM. 

 

  • Ensure capacity development of all national staff including identification of opportunities to participate in training and workshops for professional development and skills development.

 

  • Assist the PM in the management of the Dam Safety and Advisory Panel member’s contracts to ensure that Concessional Financers’ requirements are adhered to during project implementation. Assist the PM in convening Dam Safety and Advisory Panel meetings, visits and progress meetings in accordance with the project agreements.

 

  • Assist the PM in the management of the Lender’s Technical Advisor (LTA) contract to ensure that Concessional Financers’ requirements are adhered to during project implementation. In accordance with the terms of contract, assist the PM to manage the LTA’s  input, review and advice, quaterly and six-monthly site visits, and facilitate discussions with relevant project stakeholders and CFPs.

 

  • Assist the PM in the management and support the interface between LTA and Tina Hydropower Limited to complete submission of the utilization requests and supporting documents to ensure timely provision of the Technical Advisor’s Certificate in accordance with the Facilities Agreement.

 

Project Reporting

 

  • Assist the PM to ensure the reporting obligations of the Project Office are fulfilled, on time and of the required standard, including establishing an appropriate communications protocol, reporting format and processes for timely delivery. The project reports include overall quarterly progress reports, mid-term review, completion report, and other reports as required by the project agreements. The Project Office is responsible for collecting all relevant reporting inputs to complete the overall quarterly progress report, including those from Tina Hydropower Limited and Solomon Power. 

 

  • Assist the PM to update and implement the Project Operations Manual for the Project Office and coordinate the update and implementation of the Project Operations Manual for Tina Hydropower Limited, as necessary by obtaining consents of the relevant stakeholders and no objection from the relevant CFPs.

 

  • Assist the PM to lead the Project Office and coordinate key project stakeholders’ participation in CFPs periodic implementation support missions.

 

Resource Management

 

  • Assist the PM to ensure transparent, accurate and organized financial management of Project Office.

 

  • Assist the PM in his role to oversee the Project Office budget and be accountable for the funds provided to the Project Office by the CFPs, Solomon Islands Government, and other development partners as relevant.

 

  • Assist the PM to lead preparation of the Annual Work Plan and Budget for the Project Office by closely aligning with the scheduled activities of Tina Hydropower Limited for the Hydropower facility and access road and Solomon Power for the transmission line. Liaise with the Deputy Project Manager, the Environmental and Social Safeguards Manager and the Financial and Commercial advisor and assist the PM to prepare the Annual Work Plan and Budget with all relevant inputs from Project Office staff and consultants. The Annual Work Plan and Budget is due to the relevant parties not later than 30th September of each calendar year.

 

  • Assist the PM in the coordination activities with the Financial and Commercial Advisor to ensure timely preparation of Tina Hydropower Limited Annual Work Plan and Budget for the Hydropower facility and access road.

 

  • Assist the PM to lead the Project Office’s input to Ministry of Mines, Energy and Rural Electrification for its national annual development budget bid for the counterpart financing required to cover the Project Office’s operational costs. The input is to be managed in close coordination with the Deputy Project Manager. The budget bid to reach MMERE by 31st July each year. 

 

  • Assist the PM to ensure that the Project Office funds are audited on an annual basis in accordance with the project agreements.

Specific Deliverables of contract and Key Dates

These deliverables are the responsibility of the Operations Manager with support from Deputy PM and the PM.

Assignment Title: Grid Modernization and Submarine Cable Interconnection Study

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): KN-MPIEU-528498-CS-CDS

 

The Government of Saint Kitts and Nevis has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Preparation Grant for the Caribbean Resilient Renewable Energy Infrastructure Investment Facility – SOP2, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

The consulting services (“the Services”) include a study that shall explicitly address the climate and disaster-risk vulnerabilities typical of Small Island Developing States (SIDS), including hurricane and cyclone resilience of grid and submarine cable infrastructure, seismic and volcanic hazard exposure characteristic of the Lesser Antilles, and regional energy-security cooperation.

 

The assignment will be for a duration of 10 months and shall deliver a technically robust, investment-ready roadmap for modernizing the electrical grids of Saint Kitts and Nevis and interconnecting them via submarine cable, enabling full integration of renewable energy — including the proposed 30–50 MW geothermal plant, utility-scale solar PV, wind, and battery energy storage systems (BESS) — into a resilient, climate-responsive grid. Specific objectives include:

  • Grid Modernization: assess and redesign transmission and distribution infrastructure on both islands, including reconfiguration to a 69 kV ring topology, to reduce losses, improve reliability, and prepare the network for high renewable penetration.
