1. Background and Context

1.1 Country and Sector Context

The Federation of Saint Kitts and Nevis operates two independent electrical systems: Saint Kitts (SKELEC), with approximately 53 MW of installed generating capacity and 30 MW peak demand, and Nevis (NEVLEC), with approximately 19.3 MW of installed capacity and 11.5 MW peak demand. Both systems experience high losses —  approximately 8.85 % in St. Kitts and 8.8% in Nevis — and remain heavily dependent on diesel generation, resulting in elevated electricity costs, exposure to fuel-price volatility, and constrained capacity to absorb variable renewable energy.

1.2 Policy Framework and Rationale

Anchored in the Revised National Energy Policy and the Federation's Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC), the Government is committed to achieving 100% renewable electricity generation by 2030 and reducing economy-wide CO emissions by 61% relative to 2010 levels, drawing substantially on Nevis's geothermal potential together with utility-scale solar, wind, and battery energy storage.

Realizing these targets requires comprehensive grid modernization on both islands, a submarine cable interconnection linking the two systems, and integration of the proposed 30–50 MW Nevis geothermal plant. This assignment is financed under the World Bank's Caribbean Resilient Renewable Energy Infrastructure Investment Facility (RREIIF) and the Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP), and builds on prior feasibility studies and Environmental and Social Impact Assessments (ESIAs) commissioned by SKELEC, NEVLEC, Ministry of Sustainability, and the Energy Unit, as well as regional frameworks such as the OECS Decade for Sustainable Energy and the CARICOM Energy Policy.

1.3 SIDS Climate and Disaster-Risk Context

The Study shall explicitly address the climate and disaster-risk vulnerabilities typical of Small Island Developing States (SIDS), including hurricane and cyclone resilience of grid and submarine cable infrastructure, seismic and volcanic hazard exposure characteristic of the Lesser Antilles, and regional energy-security cooperation.

2. Objectives

2.1 Main Study Goals

The assignment will deliver a technically robust, investment-ready roadmap for modernizing the electrical grids of Saint Kitts and Nevis and interconnecting them via submarine cable, enabling full integration of renewable energy — including the proposed 30–50 MW geothermal plant, utility-scale solar PV, wind, and battery energy storage systems (BESS) — into a resilient, climate-responsive grid. Specific objectives include:

  • Grid Modernization: assess and redesign transmission and distribution infrastructure on both islands, including reconfiguration to a 69 kV ring topology, to reduce losses, improve reliability, and prepare the network for high renewable penetration.
  • Geothermal Integration: evaluate and specify transmission and substation requirements for delivering up to 50 MW of geothermal generation to both islands.
  • Submarine and Terrestrial Cable Interconnection: develop a technical, economically, and environmentally sound interconnection plan, including demonstrated technology and voltage selection, route selection, redundancy analysis, cable protection, terrestrial corridor works, and landing-point substation design.
  • Smart Grid and Digitalization: Design the SCADA architecture and associated Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI), Distributed Energy Resource Management Systems (DERMS), cybersecurity protocols, and integration pathways for electric vehicles (EV’s and energy storage
  • Preliminary Environmental and Social Assessment: Prepare preliminary E&S studies for the 1) submarine cable and terrestrial route survey design, and 2) transmission ring topology and substation design. Ensure full compliance with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), Environmental, Health and Safety Guidelines (EHSGs), and international technical standards (IEC, IEEE, ICPC).
  • Risk and Climate Resilience: establish a risk management framework (register, quantification, escalation, contingency planning) and a climate vulnerability assessment covering extreme-weather and geohazard resilience.
  • Capacity Building: transfer technical knowledge to SKELEC, NEVLEC, and government agencies through structured training and documentation.

2.2 Key Expected Outcomes

  • Technical specifications of Tender Package: a complete suite of technical specifications of procurement packages for grid upgrades, geothermal integration, and interconnection works, including technical specifications, cost estimates, implementation phasing, risk allocation considerations, and documentation suitable for inclusion in tender and financing processes.

 

  • Detailed Technical Specifications: engineering design concepts and digital modernization strategies enabling efficient, secure dispatch of renewable energy at all scales, independently reviewed prior to procurement (see Section 3.7).
  • Preliminary Environmental and Social Assessment: consistent with World Bank ESF and international best practices, including marine, terrestrial, and third party-infrastructure considerations.
  • Stakeholder Engagement and Inclusion: consultation records, gender and vulnerability assessments, and a result-based monitoring and evaluation framework.
  • Capacity Building and Knowledge Transfer: structured programs for local utilities and government agencies to ensure sustainability and technical self-reliance.

2.3 Intended Users and Stakeholders

  • Government Ministries and Agencies: Ministry of Public Infrastructure, Energy and Utilities; the Energy Unit; Ministry of Finance; and Ministry of Environment and Transport, for policy development, budgeting, and regulatory oversight.
  • State-Owned Utilities: SKELEC and NEVLEC, for technical implementation, grid operation, and asset management.
  • Private Developers and Investors: geothermal, solar, wind, and Power-to-X developers requiring clear interconnection requirements and grid expansion plans to mobilize project finance.
  • International Financing Partners: the World Bank and other multilateral development banks, requiring transparent, data-backed project documents that comply with fiduciary and safeguard standards.
  • Local Communities and Civil Society: benefiting from inclusive consultation, improved energy services, disaster resilience, and employment opportunities.
  • Additional Institutional Stakeholders (per prior study mapping): building on the stakeholder mapping conducted under the prior GCF-financed T&D/EV study, the Development Control Planning Board, Department of Physical Planning (Nevis), Ministry of Sustainable Development (including the National Designated Authority), Eastern Caribbean Central Bank, St. Kitts and Nevis Chamber of Industry and Commerce, licensed vehicle importers, and Clarence Fitzroy Bryant College, among others, shall be consulted as relevant to grid modernization and EV-charging integration.

3. Scope of Services

The scope is organized into clearly separated packages of work, consistent with international practice for terrestrial and subsea interconnector studies: desktop review, route/technology assessment, geophysical and geotechnical investigation, environmental and social screening, engineering design, cost estimation, procurement support, and implementation planning. The land-based (terrestrial) and marine (subsea) elements of the interconnection are treated as distinct workstreams throughout, reflecting their different technical inputs, approval pathways, and risk profiles.

3.1 Grid Modernization — Saint Kitts and Nevis

  • Conduct a full audit of transmission and distribution assets on both islands — substations, feeders, transformers, and protection/control systems — including load-flow analysis, capacity-constraint identification, and power-quality/harmonic measurements.
  • Redesign the 11 kV networks from radial to loop/ring configuration, establishing a 69 kV ring on both St. Kitts and Nevis, with conductor sizing optimization and integration points for utility-scale solar, storage, and EV-charging infrastructure.
  • Design new primary substations and switching stations — 69/11 kV (St. Kitts) and 11/69 kV (Nevis) — for submarine cable interconnection, with SCADA and protection systems integrated with existing facilities.
  • Specify dedicated transmission lines, substation requirements, and conduct grid-stability/voltage-regulation studies for geothermal plant connection.
  • Conduct a grid-code gap analysis against Caribbean and World Bank standards and propose updated grid codes and performance standards (SAIDI, SAIFI, ENS) for renewable integration, including fault ride-through requirements.
  • Define power-system modelling software and scenarios, including N-1/N-2 contingency analysis, renewable-penetration cases, and minimum/maximum load conditions.
  •  Review and Build on Prior Assessment: incorporate and validate the findings of the prior T&D Efficiency and Vulnerability Assessment (August 2025), including its recommended system upgrades (reactive compensation, advanced metering infrastructure, reconductoring of low-capacity feeders, SCADA and automated switching, and double-busbar 11 kV switchboard replacement), to avoid duplicating previously completed diagnostic work.

3.2 Submarine Cable Interconnection

The following sub-sections set out the marine interconnection scope in the level of technical detail expected of a tender ready, internationally benchmarked TOR (consistent with practice on comparable World Bank-financed interconnectors, and close gaps identified through comparison against ICPC/CIGRE industry guidance.

3.2.1 Technology and Voltage Selection

The Consultant shall not assume the voltage level or transmission technology. Rather, the Consultant shall demonstrate, through a documented technical and economic comparison, the recommended choice of AC versus HVDC transmission and the associated voltage level for the ≈ 15–20 km strait crossing, considering:

  • Capital and lifecycle cost comparison between HVAC and HVDC options at candidate voltage levels;
  • Technical suitability given the crossing distance, load profile, and future expansion (including eventual OECS/CARICOM multi-country interoperability);
  • Reactive power compensation requirements and cable charging-current constraints for the AC case;
  • Converter station footprint, cost, and maintenance implications for the HVDC case;
  • A reasoned recommendation, with the basis for the recommendation presented transparently for review by the Client, World Bank, and independent design reviewer (Section 3.7).

3.2.2 Route Selection, Marine Survey and Geohazard Screening

Conduct marine geotechnical and bathymetric surveys of three candidate routes:

    • Route 1: Charlestown–Basseterre;
    • Route 2: Cades Bay–Frigate Bay;
    • Route 3: Cades Bay–Majors Bay;

including shore-approach and beach-profile assessments and landing-point selection. Survey and screening work shall follow a staged approach — desktop screening, geophysical survey, then geotechnical confirmation — and shall meet the following minimum requirements so that competing bids are technically comparable:

  • Geophysical survey toolset: multibeam echosounder (bathymetry), side-scan sonar (seabed features/obstacles), sub-bottom profiler (sub-surface stratigraphy), and magnetometer (ferrous object/UXO screening), with a stated corridor width and survey resolution for each candidate route.
  • Geotechnical investigation: vibro-core or piston-core sampling (and cone penetration testing (CPT) where warranted) along the shortlisted route at intervals sufficient to characterize burial conditions, with a defined laboratory and in-situ testing regime to guide burial depth, trenching/ploughing method, and tooling selection.
  • Geohazard screening: explicit assessment of slope stability, seismicity, and sediment mobility/scour along the route corridor, reflecting the volcanic setting and steep nearshore bathymetry of the Narrows/Nevis Channel. This shall be a distinct deliverable and shall not be treated as implicitly covered by the bathymetric survey.

3.2.3 Cable Design, Redundancy and Protection

  • Perform combined system modelling of St. Kitts and Nevis — power-transfer scenarios, dynamic stability, short-circuit analysis, and protection coordination for interconnected operation.
  • Specify detailed technical requirements for the submarine cable, including installation/burial depth, minimum bend radius, tension limits, conductor type and rating, fiber-optic integration, reactive compensation requirements (as applicable), spare-cable provision, and repair/recovery strategy.

Cable security and physical protection: the design basis shall address anchor-strike and third party-interference (including deliberate sabotage) risk mitigation, including burial depth as a protective measure, declaration of a cable protection zone, and provisions for route monitoring, consistent with the resilience objectives of the Study.

3.2.4 Existing Infrastructure, Crossings and Third-Party Interests

The Consultant shall carry out a survey of existing seabed and nearshore infrastructure and third-party interests along candidate routes, including:

  • Existing telecommunications cables and other subsea infrastructure, with proposed crossing methodology and draft crossing-agreement provisions consistent with ICPC-recommended practice;
  • Vessel anchorages, designated anchoring areas, and shipping lanes;
  • Marine protected areas and other designated or proposed conservation zones.

3.2.5 Landing-Point Substations

Design a transmission ring topology linking major load centres and planned power-plant sites, with landing-point substations (St. Kitts: 69/11 kV; Nevis: 11/69 kV) featuring switching, control/protection, and SCADA integration. Prepare capital cost estimates, financial analysis (NPV, IRR, sensitivity), and a procurement strategy with technical specifications.

  • Reference Prior Interconnection Analysis: review and update, as appropriate, the prior study’s preliminary 33 kV express-feeder interconnection concept between Needsmust Power Station (St. Kitts) and Prospect Power Station (Nevis), including its indicative capital cost range (USD 3.0–5.1 million) and estimated fuel-displacement benefit (approximately 1.03 million litres/year), when evaluating and selecting the recommended voltage level and route for the submarine cable interconnection.

3.3 Terrestrial Cable and Transmission Works

The terrestrial component of the interconnection extends beyond the substation-to-landing-point interface and shall be scoped explicitly, covering:

  • Corridor mapping and route assessment for terrestrial cable and overhead transmission segments, including constructability constraints;
  • Design standards for terrestrial segments, and applicable undergrounding/duct-bank standards for cable sections;
  • Right-of-way and wayleave/easement identification and acquisition support, including engagement with private landowners and public authorities along the terrestrial corridor;
  • Utility and infrastructure crossings (roads, drainage, other utilities) and associated permitting requirements;
  • Trenching, ducting, and civil works specifications for terrestrial cable sections, including reinstatement requirements.

3.4 Integration Readiness Analysis

  • Assess system capacity to absorb solar PV, wind, BESS, electric vehicles (EVs), and Power-to-X projects.
  • Develop interconnection standards and operational protocols for hydrogen production and broader sector coupling.
  • Analyze regional expansion options for future multi-country interoperability with neighbouring OECS/CARICOM grids.
  • Align with EV Transition Policy and Prior EV Roadmap: ensure EV integration standards and charging-infrastructure provisions are consistent with the St. Kitts and Nevis EV Transition Policy (2024–2033) and build upon, rather than duplicate, the phased short/medium/long-term targets, financial incentives, and charging-infrastructure recommendations of the prior EV Integration Roadmap.

3.5 Preliminary Environmental and Social Impact Assessment

Given the available budget under the Preparation Grant (Section 7), this activity is scoped as a preliminary, scoping-level ESIA rather than a full ESIA. Its purpose is to screen environmental and social risks, identify data gaps, and establish an ESMP framework sufficient to inform Project design and the subproject pipeline. A full ESIA meeting Environmental and Social Standards (ESS) requirements, including detailed field-based marine surveys where warranted, shall be completed under the Follow-on Legal Agreement once the Project scope and financing are confirmed. The Consultant shall clearly flag, within the Inception Report, which of the activities below are deliverable at preliminary/desk-based level within this budget, and which would require additional field survey budget to complete to full-ESIA standard.

  • Undertake field-based marine ecosystem mapping and biodiversity assessment (fish, sea turtles, marine mammals), explicitly integrating climate-change stressors and assessing construction- and operational-phase impacts — including underwater noise, sedimentation, and water quality — with corresponding mitigation and monitoring measures.
  • Assess electromagnetic field (EMF) effects of the submarine cable on EMF-sensitive species (e.g. rays, sharks, sea turtles) as a distinct line item in the ESIA, consistent with recognized practice for international offshore cable ESIAs.
  • Incorporate the findings of the crossing/third party-infrastructure survey (Section 3.2.4) into the ESIA and ESMP, including mitigation measures and crossing-agreement provisions.
  • Conduct terrestrial and substation-site assessments — visual impact, soil/groundwater quality, and vegetation/wildlife habitat — along with a beach-profile assessment of the cable corridors.
  • Design and implement a stakeholder engagement program — public workshops, focus groups, and bilateral meetings with fishermen, tourism operators, communities, and government — ensuring project data is shared proactively with stakeholders and that community-facing engagement materials incorporate input from the Constituency Empowerment Unit.
  • Carry out socio-economic analysis of effects on fishing and tourism, local employment, and community access/navigation, with a Gender Analysis and cumulative-impact and ecosystem-services valuation and prepare an Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP) with mitigation hierarchy, monitoring indicators with targets and budgets, quarterly reporting, and a grievance redress mechanism.

3.6 Economic Analysis, Risk Management and Digital Tools

  • Conduct economic and financial analysis for each project component and the project overall — cost-benefit analysis of alternative technical solutions (including the AC/HVDC comparison in Section 3.2.1), 25–30-year financial modelling, ERR/NPV/IRR, tariff-impact scenarios, and an assessment of climate/concessional finance options available for SIDS.
  • Establish a project risk register (technical, financial, environmental, social, institutional) with mitigation strategies, contingency plans specific to submarine cables, geothermal integration, and local supply chain, and escalation protocols.
  • Apply GIS-based planning with georeferenced data for all infrastructure components and, where feasible, a digital twin of the grid and interconnection for scenario analysis and operator training.

3.7 Independent Design Review (Owner's Engineer Function)

Prior to finalization of procurement specifications for the submarine cable and associated works, the technical design shall undergo an independent design review by a qualified party separate from the core design team, consistent with practice on comparable World Bank-financed interconnectors. The independent review shall cover:

  • Verification of the technology/voltage selection basis and supporting economic analysis (Section 3.2.1);
  • Verification of route, survey, and geohazard findings and their translation into the design basis;
  • Review of redundancy, protection, and cable-security provisions;
  • Review of cost estimates and procurement packaging strategy for reasonableness and completeness.

The Consultant shall budget for and coordinate this review, incorporate review findings prior to submission of final procurement documents, and document the resolution of any review comments.

3.8 Procurement and Capacity Building

  • Undertake market sounding for submarine cable supply and installation logistics and prepare a packaging strategy for turnkey or split contracts — with risk allocation and local-content requirements — plus procurement templates and technical specifications aligned with World Bank Standard Bidding Documents.
  • Incorporate technology-transfer objectives and training requirements into contract specifications and establish anti-corruption safeguards and complaint-handling protocols.
  • Develop a capacity-building plan, train-the-trainer program, and a digital documentation repository for SKELEC, NEVLEC, and relevant government agencies, and facilitate regional knowledge-sharing (e.g. CARILEC, CCREEE).
  • Build on Existing EV Training Program: coordinate the capacity-building plan and train-the-trainer program with the existing EV Integration Training Program (led by TT PV Solar Ltd., targeting certification of 20 technicians by 2033), extending it to cover grid-modernization and interconnection-specific skills rather than duplicating the existing curriculum.

3.9 Implementation Readiness and Transition Planning

  • Develop a phased implementation roadmap and a detailed first-year action plan.
  • Design an institutional strengthening and transition plan, including staff recruitment, training, and organizational changes needed to operate the modernized/interconnected grid.
  • Identify and prepare for pre-investment activities — surveys, permits, and procurement actions — required to move directly into implementation.
  • Support Recommended Institutional Reforms: as part of the transition plan, support the Client in advancing the institutional reforms identified in the prior study — establishment of a Public Utilities Commission for unified regulatory oversight, formation of an Electric Vehicle Council, and instituting a Grid Modernization Cross-Functional Task Force — and align the phased implementation roadmap with these bodies’ mandates.

project_name: Dominican Republic Emergency Response and Resilience Project
notice_text:
SOLICITUD DE EXPRESIONES DE INTERÉS. SERVICIOS DE CONSULTORÍA

República Dominicana

Proyecto de Respuesta a Emergencias y Resiliencia de la República Dominicana

Préstamo No.: 9473-DO

Título del Trabajo:  Formulación de Instrumentos Regionales y Municipales de Ordenamiento Territorial y Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres. Región Valdesia y Región Higuamo.

No. de Referencia: DO-MEPYD-475964-CS-QCBS

El Gobierno de la República Dominicana ha recibido financiamiento del Banco Mundial para cubrir el costo del Proyecto de Respuesta a Emergencias y Resiliencia de la República Dominicana a través del Ministerio de la Presidencia y tiene la intención de aplicar parte de los fondos a la contratación de servicios de consultoría.

Los servicios de consultoría ("los Servicios") comprenden la formulación de los Planes Regionales de Ordenamiento y Desarrollo Territorial (PRODT) de las regiones Valdesia y Higuamo; siete (7) Planes Municipales de Ordenamiento Territorial (PMOT) de nueva formulación: tres (3) en Valdesia, correspondientes a Bajos de Haina, Baní y San Gregorio de Nigua; y cuatro (4) en Higuamo, correspondientes a Guayacanes, Hato Mayor, Sabana de la Mar y Monte Plata.

Además, comprenden la revisión, actualización, complementación, apoyo o armonización de cuatro (4) instrumentos municipales existentes o en formulación: dos (2) en Valdesia, correspondientes a San Cristóbal y San José de Ocoa, y dos (2) en Higuamo, correspondientes a San Pedro de Macorís y Yamasá; la formulación de cinco (5) Instrumentos de Delimitación de Suelo Urbano (IDSU), tres (3) en Valdesia, para Villa Altagracia, Yaguate y Nizao, y dos (2) en Higuamo, para Bayaguana y Sabana Grande de Boyá; nueve (9) Estrategias Territoriales de Reducción del Riesgo de Desastres y Adaptación al Cambio Climático, cinco (5) en Valdesia y cuatro (4) en Higuamo; y dos (2) Normas Subsidiarias Regionales de Planificación, una para cada región, con determinaciones territorializadas para doce (12) municipios, en un período de catorce (14) meses calendario, conforme al alcance establecido en los Términos de Referencia. Esta descripción es de carácter general; el detalle de los alcances y especificaciones técnicas se encuentra en los Términos de Referencia (TDR).

El Ministerio de la Presidencia ahora invita a las firmas consultoras elegibles ("Consultores") a indicar su interés en proporcionar los Servicios. Los Consultores interesados deben proporcionar información que demuestre que tienen las calificaciones requeridas y la experiencia relevante para prestar los Servicios. Los criterios de preselección son:

  • Actividad principal, experiencia y trayectoria de la firma. Se requiere una firma con al menos cinco (5) años de experiencia comprobable en el desarrollo de proyectos, planes o políticas relacionados con el ordenamiento y desarrollo territorial en las escalas nacional, regional, municipal y/o de desarrollo urbano. Asimismo, deberá acreditar experiencia específica en la formulación de instrumentos regionales o supramunicipales y de instrumentos municipales de ordenamiento territorial que incorporen zonificación, regulación del uso del suelo, cartografía, normativa y mecanismos de implementación, incluyendo experiencia en la ejecución simultánea de instrumentos correspondientes a distintos niveles de gobierno. Asimismo, deberá demostrar experiencia reciente, adquirida durante los últimos diez (10) años, en gestión del riesgo de desastres y adaptación al cambio climático, acreditada mediante al menos tres (3) contratos o proyectos relevantes o siete (7) años de experiencia institucional acumulada, incluyendo análisis multiamenaza, modelación hidrológico-hidráulica y sísmica, integración de escenarios climáticos y articulación de resultados con instrumentos de ordenamiento territorial e inversión pública.
  • Experiencia específica y comparabilidad de proyectos. La firma deberá acreditar al menos tres (3) proyectos similares en alcance, complejidad, niveles de gobierno y extensión geográfica, ejecutados satisfactoriamente. En conjunto, los proyectos deberán incluir: (i) al menos una experiencia en planificación regional, supramunicipal o de escala territorial equivalente; (ii) al menos una experiencia en formulación o actualización de instrumentos municipales con zonificación, cartografía y normativa de uso del suelo; y (iii) al menos una experiencia que integre gestión del riesgo de desastres, adaptación al cambio climático o Evaluación Ambiental Estratégica. Un mismo contrato podrá ser utilizado para acreditar simultáneamente más de uno de los requisitos de experiencia específica descritos anteriormente, siempre que la documentación presentada permita verificar claramente cada aspecto requerido. Las experiencias deberán permitir verificar, según corresponda, planificación regional y municipal, instrumentos normativos de uso del suelo, información geoespacial, participación territorial, fortalecimiento institucional, portafolios de inversión y estrategias de implementación.
  • Capacidad técnica, organizativa y operativa. La firma deberá demostrar capacidad técnica y de gestión para trabajar de forma simultánea en dos regiones con dinámicas territoriales diferenciadas, manteniendo coordinación técnica, control de calidad, presencia en territorio, gestión documental, producción cartográfica, participación y revisión de productos en paralelo, detallando las capacidades institucionales y herramientas utilizadas por la firma para la gestión de proyectos, producción cartográfica y administración de información.
  • Correspondencia con el alcance de la consultoría. La correspondencia será valorada mediante el análisis integrado de la experiencia y las capacidades institucionales acreditadas frente a la complejidad, escala y condiciones de ejecución de los servicios requeridos. Se considerará la capacidad demostrada para desarrollar de manera simultánea y articulada instrumentos regionales, supramunicipales y municipales de naturaleza y alcance equivalentes a los PRODT, PMOT, IDSU y Normas Subsidiarias Regionales de Planificación previstos en esta consultoría, así como Estrategias Territoriales de Reducción del Riesgo de Desastres y Adaptación al Cambio Climático; procesos participativos y de coordinación multiactor; formulación normativa; gestión de información territorial y cartográfica; Evaluación Ambiental Estratégica; fortalecimiento institucional; y productos de implementación.

Los servicios se prestarán en idioma español e implican presencia activa en el territorio de las regiones Valdesia e Higuamo y en el Distrito Nacional, República Dominicana.

Nota: Los Expertos Clave no serán evaluados en la etapa de preselección.

Para estos fines la firma consultora deberá remitir la documentación de forma clara, estructurada, verificable y directamente vinculada con los criterios de preselección establecidos en la presente Solicitud de Expresiones de Interés (SEI). El documento principal no deberá exceder de cuarenta (40) páginas. Los documentos legales y los soportes documentales presentados para acreditar la experiencia y capacidad declaradas no se computarán dentro de este límite y deberán incorporarse como anexos debidamente identificados, paginados y referenciados. La documentación técnica de soporte no deberá exceder de ciento cincuenta (150) páginas para una firma consultora individual. En caso de APCA, consorcio, joint venture o asociación equivalente, el límite será de ciento cincuenta (150) páginas por cada integrante que acredite experiencia o capacidad técnica, organizativa u operativa relevante para los criterios de preselección. El registro mercantil, la nómina de accionistas y los documentos legales equivalentes no se computarán dentro de estos límites de páginas.

La documentación requerida es la siguiente:

  • Carta de expresión de interés, con datos generales de la firma consultora (firmada y sellada).
  • Detalle de experiencia directa de la firma consultora donde se evidencie: actividad principal y años en el negocio, experiencia relevante, capacidad técnica y de gestión de la firma consultora de acuerdo con los requerimientos arriba mencionados. Para cada experiencia declarada deberá indicarse de manera organizada, como mínimo, el nombre del contrato o proyecto, cliente y país, fechas de ejecución, monto contractual, alcance, rol desempeñado por la firma o integrante de la APCA, productos o actividades efectivamente ejecutados, escala territorial, criterio o criterios de preselección que acredita y referencia exacta del soporte documental presentado.
  • Estructura organizativa general de la Firma Consultora o APCA, con una breve descripción de sus áreas técnicas, capacidades institucionales y recursos permanentes relevantes para la consultoría. En esta etapa no deberán presentarse CV ni se evaluarán las calificaciones de expertos individuales.
  • Registro mercantil actualizado o equivalente en su país de origen.
  • Nómina de accionistas o documento equivalente en su país de origen.

Nota: Toda la documentación que se presente deberá estar en idioma español.

La lista corta estará integrada por un mínimo de cinco (5) y un máximo de ocho (8) firmas consultoras.

Se llama la atención de los Consultores interesados sobre la Sección III, párrafos 3.14, 3.16 y 3.17 de las “Regulaciones de Adquisiciones para Prestatarios en Proyectos de Inversión del Banco Mundial, actualizadas a noviembre de 2020 (“Regulaciones de Adquisiciones”), que establece la política del Banco Mundial sobre conflictos de intereses.

Los Consultores podrán asociarse con otras firmas para mejorar sus calificaciones y deberán indicar claramente si la asociación se presenta como APCA (joint venture, consorcio o asociación equivalente) o como subconsultoría. En caso de APCA, todos sus integrantes serán conjunta y solidariamente responsables de la totalidad del contrato, si resultan seleccionados.

Se puede obtener más información durante el horario de oficina de 08:00 a 16:00 horas, en las oficinas de este Viceministerio ubicadas en la calle César Nicolás Penson núm. 48, Distrito Nacional, Santo Domingo, República Dominicana, o mediante comunicación escrita dirigida al correo electrónico adquisicioneseyr@minpre.gob.do.

Asimismo, deberá acreditar experiencia específica en la formulación de instrumentos regionales o supramunicipales y de instrumentos municipales de ordenamiento territorial que incorporen zonificación, regulación del uso del suelo, cartografía, normativa y mecanismos de implementación, incluyendo experiencia en la ejecución simultánea de instrumentos correspondientes a distintos niveles de gobierno. Asimismo, deberá demostrar experiencia reciente, adquirida durante los últimos diez (10) años, en gestión del riesgo de desastres y adaptación al cambio climático, acreditada mediante al menos tres (3) contratos o proyectos relevantes o siete (7) años de experiencia institucional acumulada, incluyendo análisis multiamenaza, modelación hidrológico-hidráulica y sísmica, integración de escenarios climáticos y articulación de resultados con instrumentos de ordenamiento territorial e inversión pública
  • Experiencia específica y comparabilidad de proyectos. La firma deberá acreditar al menos tres (3) proyectos similares en alcance, complejidad, niveles de gobierno y extensión geográfica, ejecutados satisfactoriamente. En conjunto, los proyectos deberán incluir: (i) al menos una experiencia en planificación regional, supramunicipal o de escala territorial equivalente; (ii) al menos una experiencia en formulación o actualización de instrumentos municipales con zonificación, cartografía y normativa de uso del suelo; y (iii) al menos una experiencia que integre gestión del riesgo de desastres, adaptación al cambio climático o Evaluación Ambiental Estratégica. Un mismo contrato podrá ser utilizado para acreditar simultáneamente más de uno de los requisitos de experiencia específica descritos anteriormente, siempre que la documentación presentada permita verificar claramente cada aspecto requerido. Las experiencias deberán permitir verificar, según corresponda, planificación regional y municipal, instrumentos normativos de uso del suelo, información geoespacial, participación territorial, fortalecimiento institucional, portafolios de inversión y estrategias de implementación.
  • Capacidad técnica, organizativa y operativa. La firma deberá demostrar capacidad técnica y de gestión para trabajar de forma simultánea en dos regiones con dinámicas territoriales diferenciadas, manteniendo coordinación técnica, control de calidad, presencia en territorio, gestión documental, producción cartográfica, participación y revisión de productos en paralelo, detallando las capacidades institucionales y herramientas utilizadas por la firma para la gestión de proyectos, producción cartográfica y administración de información.
  • Correspondencia con el alcance de la consultoría. La correspondencia será valorada mediante el análisis integrado de la experiencia y las capacidades institucionales acreditadas frente a la complejidad, escala y condiciones de ejecución de los servicios requeridos. Se considerará la capacidad demostrada para desarrollar de manera simultánea y articulada instrumentos regionales, supramunicipales y municipales de naturaleza y alcance equivalentes a los PRODT, PMOT, IDSU y Normas Subsidiarias Regionales de Planificación previstos en esta consultoría, así como Estrategias Territoriales de Reducción del Riesgo de Desastres y Adaptación al Cambio Climático; procesos participativos y de coordinación multiactor; formulación normativa; gestión de información territorial y cartográfica; Evaluación Ambiental Estratégica; fortalecimiento institucional; y productos de implementación.

Los servicios se prestarán en idioma español e implican presencia activa en el territorio de las regiones Cibao Noroeste y Cibao Sur y en el Distrito Nacional, República Dominicana.

Nota: Los Expertos Clave no serán evaluados en la etapa de preselección.

Para estos fines la firma consultora deberá remitir la documentación de forma clara, estructurada, verificable y directamente vinculada con los criterios de preselección establecidos en la presente Solicitud de Expresiones de Interés (SEI). El documento principal no deberá exceder de cuarenta (40) páginas. Los documentos legales y los soportes documentales presentados para acreditar la experiencia y capacidad declaradas no se computarán dentro de este límite y deberán incorporarse como anexos debidamente identificados, paginados y referenciados. La documentación técnica de soporte no deberá exceder de ciento cincuenta (150) páginas para una firma consultora individual. En caso de APCA, consorcio, joint venture o asociación equivalente, el límite será de ciento cincuenta (150) páginas por cada integrante que acredite experiencia o capacidad técnica, organizativa u operativa relevante para los criterios de preselección. El registro mercantil, la nómina de accionistas y los documentos legales equivalentes no se computarán dentro de estos límites de páginas.

La documentación requerida es la siguiente:

  • Carta de expresión de interés, con datos generales de la firma consultora (firmada y sellada).
  • Detalle de experiencia directa de la firma consultora donde se evidencie: actividad principal y años en el negocio, experiencia relevante, capacidad técnica y de gestión de la firma consultora de acuerdo con los requerimientos arriba mencionados. Para cada experiencia declarada deberá indicarse de manera organizada, como mínimo, el nombre del contrato o proyecto, cliente y país, fechas de ejecución, monto contractual, alcance, rol desempeñado por la firma o integrante de la APCA, productos o actividades efectivamente ejecutados, escala territorial, criterio o criterios de preselección que acredita y referencia exacta del soporte documental presentado.

  • Nómina de accionistas o documento equivalente en su país de origen.

Nota: Toda la documentación que se presente deberá estar en idioma español.

La lista corta estará integrada por un mínimo de cinco (5) y un máximo de ocho (8) firmas consultoras.

Se llama la atención de los Consultores interesados sobre la Sección III, párrafos 3.14, 3.16 y 3.17 de las “Regulaciones de Adquisiciones para Prestatarios en Proyectos de Inversión del Banco Mundial, actualizadas a noviembre de 2020 (“Regulaciones de Adquisiciones”), que establece la política del Banco Mundial sobre conflictos de intereses.

Los Consultores podrán asociarse con otras firmas para mejorar sus calificaciones y deberán indicar claramente si la asociación se presenta como APCA (joint venture, consorcio o asociación equivalente) o como subconsultoría. En caso de APCA, todos sus integrantes serán conjunta y solidariamente responsables de la totalidad del contrato, si resultan seleccionados.

Consultancy for Provision of Fund Management Services for the Ngwee Ngwee Ngwee Fund

MW-MOE.-574017-CS-QCBS

EOI Issue Date

28th September 2026

This request for expression of interest follows the General Procurement Notice for this Project that appeared in the United Nations Development Business (UNDB) on 31st January 2025.

The Government of the Republic of Malawi through the Ministry of Energy (MoE) has received financing from the International Development Association (IDA) and the Energy Sector Management Assistance Program (ESMAP) towards the cost of implementing the Accelerating Sustainable and Clean Energy Access Transformation in Malawi (ASCENT Malawi) Project. It is intended that part of the proceeds of the financing will be used to cover eligible payments under the contract for these consultancy services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) are intended to engage a qualified consulting firm or consortium to provide Fund Management Services for the Ngwee Ngwee Ngwee Fund (NNNF). The Fund Manager will support the Ministry of Energy in delivering ASCENT Malawi Project Components 2, 3 and 4; managing legacy Malawi Electricity Access Project (MEAP) loan collections and residual obligations; and supporting the transition and institutionalisation of the NNNF as a sustainable standalone revolving fund.

The assignment is expected to be implemented over forty-eight (48) Calendar months, from 1st January 2027 to 31st December 2030, subject to contract signature and availability of financing.

The objective of the assignment is to provide specialised fund management services that enable timely, compliant and well-secured financing to eligible Participating Organisations; ensure sound portfolio, fiduciary, safeguards, data and risk management; protect the Fund’s creditor rights; support achievement of ASCENT energy-access and market-development results; and strengthen systems, national capacity and arrangements for the long-term sustainability of the NNNF.

The scope of work under this assignment shall include, but not be limited to:

a) Inception, portfolio takeover, reconciliation and structured handover of existing NNNF facilities, commitments, systems, records and outstanding actions;

b) Cross-cutting fund administration, including drawdown and payment review, portfolio monitoring, forecasting, records management, risk management and reporting;

c) Administration of Component 2 debt and Results-Based Financing (RBF) facilities for off-grid solar companies, including disbursements, repayments, verification interfaces, portfolio quality and recovery actions;

d) Administration of Component 3 financing and performance-linked payments for electrification of public schools and health facilities, in coordination with the ASCENT PIU technical team;

e) Administration of Component 4 clean cooking financing, including loans, repayments, security, portfolio monitoring and carbon-finance interfaces;

f) Management of loan collateral, security perfection, covenant monitoring, enforcement and recoveries, subject to Ministry approvals;

g) Management and collection of the legacy MEAP loan portfolio, including arrears, restructuring, recoveries and close-out actions;

h) Data management, monitoring, dashboards, financial and operational reconciliation, fraud and corruption controls, cybersecurity and data protection;

i) Implementation and monitoring of environmental and social requirements in accordance with the NNNF ESMS, applicable Malawi law and World Bank requirements;

j) Coordination with the Independent Verification Agent, Legal Advisor, Carbon Consultant, technical specialists and other consultants engaged by the Ministry; and

k) Support to institutionalisation of the NNNF, including governance arrangements, capitalisation options, sustainable business model, capacity development, systems transfer and final handover.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TORs) for the assignment can be found at the following websites: Ministry of Energy (https://energy.gov.mw/resources/), Ngwee Ngwee Ngwee Fund (https://www.nnnf.energy.gov.mw/resources/) and ASCENT Malawi Project (https://www.ascent.mw/resources/), or upon request through amopiha@ascent.mw copied to info@ascent.mw and austin.theu@energy.gov.mw. All requests for clarification should be sent through the above email addresses.

The MoE now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are as follows:

1. Core business of the firm(s) and years in business of not less than 5 years organizational capability and relevant experience in fund management, investment, lending, RBF/grant facilities or comparable financing programmes.

2. Relevant similar experience, which should specifically include the below:

a) Off-grid solar and clean cooking sector expertise: experience in, and understanding of, the off-grid solar and clean cooking market in Sub-Saharan Africa, including Energy-as-a-Service and PAYGo solar business models (minimum of five years), together with specific experience in, and understanding of, the Malawi off-grid solar and clean cooking market and the success factors of for-profit businesses in this sector;

b) Results-Based Financing (RBF) and grant facility management: a minimum of three years track record of structuring and managing RBF grant facilities aimed at market stimulation, ideally facilities funded by multilateral development banks, development finance institutions and/or bilateral development assistance agencies;

c) Debt and consumer financing track record: a minimum of three years track record of providing debt financing to off-grid solar and clean cooking distribution businesses and/or consumer finance businesses, including microfinance institutions;

d) Malawi presence and government/development-partner engagement: an established or committed local footprint in Malawi sufficient to manage relationships and reporting with the Government of Malawi and with RBF Grant Window and Debt Window applicants and investees and experience managing reporting relationships with government stakeholders and large development finance organisations;

e) Integration & Institutional Capability: Capacity to integrate sector expertise, financing mechanisms, and local presence, with into a coherent delivery model, supported by evidence of technical and managerial systems for coordinating RBF, debt financing, and stakeholder reporting, and scalable energy-access ability to sustain and scale operations in Malawi’s energy access sector.

3. Technical and managerial capability of the firm (provide only the structure of the organization, general qualifications, and number of key staff. Do not provide CVs of the staff. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

This Request for Expressions of Interest is open to all eligible firms as defined in the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (July 2016, as revised November 2017, August 2018, September 2023 and February 2025). Firms declared ineligible by the World Bank Group in accordance with the Bank's guidelines on Preventing and Combating Fraud and Corruption in Projects Financed by IBRD Loans and IDA Credits and Grants are not eligible to participate.

Consultants may associate with other firms in the form of a Joint Venture (JV) or sub-consultancy to enhance their qualifications. In the case of a JV, the firms should clearly identify the lead firm and the nature of the association. All partners in a joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality- and Cost-Based (QCBS) Selection method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers.

Interested firms are requested to submit an Expression of Interest containing the following information:

  • Firm Profile: organisation name, legal status, country of registration, year of establishment, core business and contact details.
  • Relevant Experience: description of similar assignments, including client, assignment title, duration, contract value, scope and role of the firm; reference contacts should be provided.

title: Consultoría para aplicar control de calidad de vuelos fotogramétricos, MDS y MDT y ortoimágenes
project_name: Dominican Republic Emergency Response and Resilience Project
notice_text:
SOLICITUD DE EXPRESIONES DE INTERÉS

SERVICIOS DE CONSULTORÍA

República Dominicana

Proyecto de Respuesta a Emergencias y Resiliencia de la República Dominicana

Préstamo No.: 9473-DO

Título del Trabajo:  Consultoría para aplicar control de calidad de vuelos fotogramétricos, MDS y MDT y ortoimágenes.

No. de Referencia: DO-MEPyD-470659-CS-QCBS

El Gobierno de la República Dominicana ha recibido financiamiento del Banco Mundial para cubrir el costo del Proyecto de Respuesta a Emergencias y Resiliencia de la República Dominicana a través del Ministerio de la Presidencia y tiene la intención de aplicar parte de los fondos a la contratación de servicios de consultoría.

Los servicios de consultoría ("los Servicios") comprenden la supervisión, verificación progresiva, control de calidad externo y validación técnica de los productos cartográficos básicos generados por el contrato de producción cartográfica del Proyecto. La firma consultora deberá revisar la correcta aplicación del aseguramiento de calidad del Proveedor del Servicio de producción y realizar las comprobaciones independientes adicionales que resulten necesarias, en gabinete y, cuando corresponda, en campo, para verificar la conformidad de los insumos, procesos, productos intermedios y productos finales con las especificaciones técnicas, estándares y criterios de aceptación aplicables.

El alcance comprende, principalmente, los vuelos fotogramétricos con captura de imágenes aéreas y datos LiDAR; puntos de fotocontrol y comprobación; orientación de imágenes y aerotriangulación; ajuste, filtrado y clasificación de nubes de puntos LiDAR; Modelos Digitales de Superficie (MDS) y Modelos Digitales del Terreno (MDT); y mosaicos de ortoimágenes digitales verdaderas (true-orthos), así como la documentación técnica, metadatos, formatos, certificados de calidad y demás respaldos asociados. La producción objeto de supervisión cubre aproximadamente 48,196.00 km² del territorio nacional, diferenciados en zona urbana (2,896.70 km²) y zona rural (45,299.30 km²). Los Servicios tendrán una duración de doce (12) meses calendario, conforme al alcance y condiciones establecidos en los Términos de Referencia (TDR). Esta descripción es de carácter general; el detalle de los alcances y especificaciones técnicas se encuentra en los TDR.

El Ministerio de la Presidencia ahora invita a las firmas consultoras elegibles ("Consultores") a indicar su interés en proporcionar los Servicios. Los Consultores interesados deben proporcionar información que demuestre que tienen las calificaciones requeridas y la experiencia relevante para prestar los Servicios. Los criterios de preselección son:

  • Actividad principal, experiencia y trayectoria de la firma. La firma consultora deberá acreditar trayectoria institucional en servicios relacionados con información geoespacial, cartografía, geodesia, fotogrametría aérea, teledetección, LiDAR, modelos digitales de elevaciones, ortoimágenes, control de calidad cartográfica, supervisión técnica o validación de productos geoespaciales. Deberá demostrar una experiencia general mínima de ocho (8) años y haber ejecutado satisfactoriamente al menos cinco (5) contratos relacionados con estos servicios durante los últimos ocho (8) años.
  • Experiencia específica y comparabilidad de proyectos. La firma deberá acreditar al menos tres (3) contratos de naturaleza comparable ejecutados satisfactoriamente durante los últimos ocho (8) años. En conjunto, dichas experiencias deberán incluir: (i) al menos dos (2) contratos con actividades de supervisión, auditoría técnica, QA/QC, validación o aceptación de productos fotogramétricos y/o LiDAR; (ii) al menos un (1) proyecto de cobertura nacional, subnacional extensa, regional o territorialmente continua; y (iii) al menos un (1) proyecto que haya comprendido productos LiDAR y modelos digitales de elevaciones, además de ortoimágenes u ortofotos. Un mismo contrato podrá acreditar más de una condición cuando su alcance lo demuestre de manera verificable. La experiencia en producción cartográfica será considerada únicamente cuando evidencie funciones sustantivas de aseguramiento o control de calidad sobre los productos generados.
  • Capacidad técnica, organizativa y operativa. La firma deberá demostrar capacidad para ejecutar revisiones concurrentes y especializadas por bloques, productos o frentes de trabajo; aplicar procedimientos de QA/QC; gestionar grandes volúmenes de imágenes aéreas, nubes de puntos LiDAR, MDS, MDT y ortoimágenes; y mantener trazabilidad documental, control de versiones y seguimiento de observaciones y subsanaciones. Deberá acreditar disponibilidad de recursos computacionales, software, licencias, infraestructura de procesamiento y almacenamiento, herramientas especializadas y mecanismos seguros de intercambio y respaldo de información, así como capacidad organizativa para iniciar oportunamente la consultoría y cumplir los tiempos de revisión previstos.
  • Correspondencia con el alcance de la consultoría. La correspondencia será valorada mediante el análisis integrado de la experiencia y las capacidades institucionales acreditadas frente a la escala y complejidad de los Servicios. Se considerará especialmente la experiencia en revisión y validación de planes de vuelo, cobertura y GSD, GNSS/IMU, control terrestre, aerotriangulación, ajuste y clasificación LiDAR, MDS/MDT, ortorrectificación, ortoimágenes verdaderas, exactitud posicional, completitud, consistencia radiométrica, formatos, metadatos y trazabilidad documental, así como la capacidad para coordinar técnicamente con el Contratante y el Proveedor del Servicio de producción preservando la independencia del control de calidad externo.

La firma consultora deberá actuar con independencia técnica respecto del Proveedor del Servicio de producción y declarar cualquier vínculo contractual, societario, comercial, técnico o profesional que pueda comprometer la objetividad de la supervisión. Los Servicios se prestarán en idioma español, en modalidad combinada de gabinete y, cuando corresponda, actividades presenciales o verificaciones de campo. La firma adjudicataria deberá disponer o establecer una oficina local en Santo Domingo durante la ejecución de la consultoría.

Nota: Los Expertos Clave no serán evaluados en la etapa de preselección y no deberán presentarse CV en esta etapa.

Para estos fines la firma consultora deberá remitir la documentación de forma clara, estructurada, verificable y directamente vinculada con los criterios de preselección establecidos en la presente Solicitud de Expresiones de Interés (SEI). El documento principal no deberá exceder de cuarenta (40) páginas. Los documentos legales y los soportes documentales presentados para acreditar la experiencia y capacidad declaradas no se computarán dentro de este límite y deberán incorporarse como anexos debidamente identificados, paginados y referenciados. La documentación técnica de soporte no deberá exceder de ciento cincuenta (150) páginas para una firma consultora individual. En caso de APCA, consorcio, joint venture o asociación equivalente, el límite será de ciento cincuenta (150) páginas por cada integrante que acredite experiencia o capacidad técnica, organizativa u operativa relevante para los criterios de preselección. El registro mercantil, la nómina de accionistas y los documentos legales equivalentes no se computarán dentro de estos límites de páginas.

La documentación requerida es la siguiente:

  • Carta de expresión de interés, con datos generales de la firma consultora (firmada y sellada).
  • Detalle de experiencia directa de la firma consultora donde se evidencie: actividad principal y años en el negocio, experiencia general y específica, capacidad técnica y de gestión de acuerdo con los criterios indicados. Para cada experiencia declarada deberá indicarse, como mínimo, el nombre del contrato o proyecto, cliente y país, fechas de ejecución, monto contractual, alcance, rol desempeñado por la firma o integrante de la APCA, productos o actividades efectivamente ejecutados, superficie o cobertura territorial, componentes fotogramétricos y/o LiDAR comprendidos, funciones de QA/QC, supervisión o validación realizadas, criterios o estándares de calidad aplicados, criterio o criterios de preselección que acredita y referencia exacta del soporte documental presentado. Para acreditar las experiencias no será necesario presentar el contrato completo; podrán aportarse únicamente las páginas pertinentes del contrato, certificaciones, actas de recepción, constancias de conformidad, informes finales aprobados u otra documentación equivalente emitida o validada por el cliente o contratante que permita verificar la experiencia declarada.
  • Estructura organizativa general de la Firma Consultora o APCA, con una breve descripción de sus áreas técnicas, capacidades institucionales, recursos permanentes, infraestructura computacional, software y mecanismos de gestión y control de calidad relevantes para la consultoría. En esta etapa no deberán presentarse CV ni se evaluarán las calificaciones de expertos individuales.
  • Declaración de independencia técnica y ausencia de conflictos de interés que puedan afectar la objetividad de la consultoría, con el compromiso de informar al Contratante cualquier posible conflicto que se identifique durante el proceso de selección o la ejecución del contrato.
  • Registro mercantil actualizado o equivalente en su país de origen.
  • Nómina de accionistas o documento equivalente en su país de origen.

Nota: Toda la documentación que se presente deberá estar en idioma español.

La lista corta estará integrada por un mínimo de cinco (5) y un máximo de ocho (8) firmas consultoras.

Se llama la atención de los Consultores interesados sobre la Sección III, párrafos 3.14, 3.16 y 3.17 de las “Regulaciones de Adquisiciones para Prestatarios en Proyectos de Inversión del Banco Mundial”, actualizadas a noviembre de 2020 (“Regulaciones de Adquisiciones”), en las que se establece la política del Banco Mundial sobre conflictos de intereses.

Los Consultores podrán asociarse con otras firmas para mejorar sus calificaciones y deberán indicar claramente si la asociación se presenta como APCA (joint venture, consorcio o asociación equivalente) o como subconsultoría. En caso de APCA, todos sus integrantes serán conjunta y solidariamente responsables de la totalidad del contrato, si resultan seleccionados.

El Consultor será seleccionado conforme al método de Selección Basada en Calidad y Costo (SBCC/QCBS), de acuerdo con las Regulaciones de Adquisiciones.

Se puede obtener más información durante el horario de oficina de 08:00 a 16:00 horas, en las oficinas de este Viceministerio ubicadas en la calle César Nicolás Penson núm. 48, Distrito Nacional, Santo Domingo, República Dominicana, o mediante comunicación escrita dirigida al correo electrónico adquisicioneseyr@minpre.gob.do.

Los TDR podrán solicitarse, sin costo, mediante comunicación dirigida al correo electrónico antes indicado, haciendo constar en el asunto la referencia del proceso, o descargarse desde el enlace correspondiente a este proceso, publicado en el Portal de Transparencia del Ministerio de la Presidencia: https://minpre.gob.do/transparencia/compras-y-contrataciones/contratacion-de-consultoria-para-aplicar-control-de-calidad-de-vuelos-fotogrametricos-mds-y-mdt-y-ortoimagenes-ref-do-mepyd-470659-cs-qcbs/.

Las expresiones de interés deben enviarse por escrito a la siguiente dirección (en persona, por correo o por correo electrónico) hasta el 26 de octubre de 2026, a las 4:00 p. m. (hora de la República Dominicana).

title: Technical Assistance to operationalize the Road Asset Management System (RAMS)
project_name: Moldova Rural Connectivity Project
notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

 

 

Country: Moldova

Name of Project: Moldova Rural Connectivity Project

Project ID: P180153

 

Assignment Title: Technical assistance for the further development of Road Asset Management System in Moldova

 

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): MRCP/CS/08

 

The Government of the Republic of Moldova has received financing from the World Bank (the “Bank” or the “WB”) in the form of a loan/credit toward the cost of the Moldova Rural Connectivity Project. The S.A. ”Administraia Naional a Drumurilor” (“NRA” or JSC “National Road Administration”), an implementing agency (the “Client”), intends to apply part of the proceeds of this loan/credit to eligible payments under the contract for which this Request for Expressions of Interest is issued.

NRA has developed and operates a Road Asset Management System (RAMS). However, there are still many unresolved issues that prevent the proper use of the RAMS as a key pillar for the further effective road investment and maintenance planning processes, such as: lack of integration/interoperability of sub systems; manual intensive data collection; fragmentation of roles in RAMS related data collection and utilization; non-clear future alignment with the road register; lack of the sufficient legal regulation.

NRA intends to retain a consultant to lay the strategic, technical, institutional, and legal groundwork for the modernization of NRA's Road Asset Management System, so that Moldova's national road network can be managed efficiently, cost-effectively, and in line with European standards. Specifically, consultant will be required to review business processes and recommend improvements; review of existing IT based tools, software, databases, etc. architecture and integration and recommendations for further improvement preparation; develop a future RAMS Roadmap; define the asset inventory scope and data governance framework required for the future RAMS; Policy Framework Development; develop a training program and conduct a number of in-person workshops covering mentioned above topics.

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained following a formal request to the Client to procurement.wb@andsa.md.

 

The NRA now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Consulting Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The Consultant will be a firm or a group of firms (JVCA[1]) with previous project experience related to Construction Supervision Services.

 

The shortlisting criteria:

The following shortlisting criteria will be applied to all consulting firms (individual company or joint venture overall) that have submitted EoI:

1. Criterion: General Firm Experience

Proven general experience and verifiable track record in providing consultancy/technical assistance related to Road Asset Management Systems (RAMSs), completed within the past ten (10) years. RAMS-related consultancy/technical assistance may cover studies; strategies; policy frameworks; institutional support; or preparation of methodologies, guidelines, and standards.

Scoring:

The Consultant shall be awarded up to 20 points based on the quality and relevance of project references.

 

2. Criterion: Development or implementation of RAMS solutions

Proven specific expertise and verifiable track record in the assignments related to development or implementation of the existing RAMS solutions, deployed on local and/or national road networks with paved and unpaved roads, completed within the past ten (10) years. For the purpose of this criterion, an assignment shall be considered completed if the RAMS solution has been fully developed and/or deployed and formally accepted by the client, regardless of subsequent maintenance or update activities.

Preference will be given to projects related to the local road networks.

Scoring:

The Consultant shall be awarded up to 40 points based on the quality and relevance of project references.

 

3. Criterion: Road network data

Proven specific expertise and verifiable track record in the assignments related to road network data survey, collection, and verification to be incorporated in a developed road database, completed within the past ten (10) years.

Scoring:

The Consultant shall be awarded up to 30 points based on the quality and relevance of project references.

 

4. Criterion: Training

Proven specific expertise and verifiable track record in delivering training related to RAMS completed within the last ten (10) years, with preference given to projects related to the local road networks.

Scoring:

The Consultant shall be awarded up to 10 points based on the quality and relevance of project references.

 

As a proof, the Consultant shall prepare a table listing following information: name of the relevant assignments, year of contract’s implementation (start year, end year), information on contract value, length of road network covered, percentage carried out by Consultant in case of association of firms and short description of main activities, contracting entity/client, country/region, contact reference (name, e-mail, phone number).

The maximum score that can be awarded to the Consultant is 100 points based on the cumulative evaluation of all criteria.

 

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

 

The submitted EOI shall not exceed 40 pages.

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-Based Selection method (QCBS) set out in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, February 2025, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.15 3.16, 3.17 and 3.18 of the abovementioned World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. 2. The objective of the consulting services (“the Services”) is to support the development and application of geospatial least-cost electrification planning approaches, including the identification of optimal combinations of grid extension, mini-grid, and standalone systems to achieve universal access objectives, and to be grounded in internationally recognized methodologies that ensure transparency, consistency, and reproducibility of analytical approaches, as well as the development or strengthening of related geospatial data systems, data governance arrangements, interoperability mechanisms, and digital decision-support tools

 

3. Scope of service”; The services to be provided under the Framework Agreement are organized into indicative service components, which describe the range of technical support that may be required

 

Individual assignments issued under the Framework Agreement may involve one or several service components, depending on the needs of the requesting Project Implementation Unit (PIU).

 

The combination and scope of services to be provided under each assignment will depend on the specific needs of the requesting PIU and the nature of the Service Request submitted to COMESA.

Service component 1:

 Development of National Electrification Analyses (NEAs).

 

Consulting firms may support participating PIUs in preparing or updating National Electrification Analyses using geospatial least-cost electrification modelling methodologies. Activities may include the collection and validation of spatial datasets, development or updating of geospatial least-cost electrification models, analysis of grid extension, mini-grid and standalone electrification options, and preparation of electrification investment planning scenarios.

 

Service component 2:

Updating Existing Electrification Plans and Models.

 

Consulting firms may assist PIUs in reviewing and updating existing electrification plans and modelling tools. Activities may include updating modelling assumptions and datasets, recalibrating electrification planning models, incorporating updated demand forecasts or policy targets, and producing revised electrification planning outputs.

Service component 3:

Spatial Data Infrastructure (SDI), Data Governance and Interoperability.

 

Consulting firms may assist PIUs in establishing or strengthening national spatial data infrastructure (SDI) systems, data governance arrangements and interoperable geospatial data platforms to support energy access planning. Activities may include assessing SDI readiness, identifying data architecture and interoperability gaps, developing data governance frameworks and standards, and establishing or enhancing geospatial data platforms, metadata catalogues and data-sharing mechanisms, including, where relevant, open-source or interoperable platforms such as GeoNode, CKAN, or equivalent tools.

 

Service component 4:

Development of Visualization and Decision-Support Platforms.

 

Consulting firms may support the development of digital platforms and tools that facilitate the analysis and dissemination of electrification planning outputs. Activities may include development of geospatial dashboards, creation of data portals for electrification planning outputs, and integration with national energy information systems.

Service component 5:

Capacity Building and Institutional Support.

 

Consulting firms may provide technical assistance and training to strengthen national capacities in geospatial electrification planning. Activities may include training on modelling methodologies and planning tools, support for data management processes, and preparation of technical guidelines and operational manuals.

 

The consulting services “Framework Agreement for Geospatial Electrification Planning and Analytical Services” include establishment for an initial period of three (3) years and may, subject to satisfactory performance, continued need, availability of financing, and any applicable approvals, be extended for up to two (2) additional one-year periods.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

 

 

Country:  MOZAMBIQUE

Project:  Mphanda Nkuwa Hydroelectric Project

Agreement: Preparation Advance No. -V522-MZ.

Assignment Title: Individual Consultancy Services to Provision Hydrologist Specialist Project Advisor for providing Project Advisory to undertaking the review of the hydrological studies of the planned Mphanda Nkuwa Hydropower Project.

 

Reference: MZ-GMNK-442364-CS-INDV

 

 

 

The Government of Mozambique (GoM) hereinafter referred to as “the Borrower” have received Advance funds from International Development Association (IDA) towards the costs of the Mphanda Nkuwa Hydroelectric Project, Preparation Phase. The funds have been channeled through the Mphanda Nkuwa Hydroelectric Project Office (GMNK) as the Project Implementation Agency, and GMNK intends to apply part of the proceeds for Consulting Services for providing Project Advisory for undertaking the review of the hydrological studies of the planned Mphanda Nkuwa Hydropower Project.

 

 

The GMNK now invites eligible Individual Consultant (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the Services. Interested Individual Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. The shortlisting criteria are:

 

  1. qualification, experience and skills in providing Project advisory services for reviewing the hydrological studies of hydropower projects;
  2. a minimum of Post Graduate Degree in the relevant hydrological disciplines and must have at least 15 years of professional experience relevant to the assignment.
  3. description of similar assignments previously carried out - must have done at least two (2) similar assignments (hydrological of hydropower advisory services), and
  4. experience of working in Sub-Sahara Africa - at least one (1) of the assignments should be in Sub-Shara Africa - and other regions.

 

Evidence shall be attached as supporting documents for the Expression of Interest.

 

Objective

 

The Project is being prepared for seeking financial support of the World Bank (the “Bank”) and therefore must comply with the World Bank Safeguards Policies and Performance Standards (see the concept project information document stage at the WB website [1]).  Accordingly, the Mphanda Nkuwa Project needs to comply with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) – Community Health and Safety (ESS4[2]). To this effect two panel of experts (PoEs) need to be formed: (i) Panel of Experts for Dam Safety (PoE-DS); and (ii) Panel of Experts for Environmental and Social Management (PoE-ESM).

Key Responsibilities/ Scope of Reviews

 

The hydrologist will:

 

  1. Review of the hydrological studies pertaining to the long-term inflow to the reservoirs, and spillway and diversion design floods with reference to international criteria. Assess the adequacy of spillway and diversion facilities, also considering increasing hydrological variability associated with global warming. Review of soil erosion data and estimate of sediment yield into the reservoirs, estimated reservoir sedimentation, and assessment of the long-term sustainable capacity that could be maintained by implementing appropriate management strategies. Review of layouts related to sediment management of the reservoirs including sediment flushing.
  2. Review of the design of spillway and tailrace facilities including flow conditions, energy dissipation and need for hydraulic modelling.
  3. Review of the designs of the diversion works, schedule and risk factors associated with diversion during construction and with the closure of diversion works at initial reservoir filling.

 

Expected Assignment Timeline

 

The assignment is for a period of six (6) years, covering project preparation, construction, and initial reservoir filling. The initial contract will be signed for a period of 2 years, with the potential for an extension to cover the full duration of preparation and implementation. The contract will be time-based, with an annual ceiling of 20 working days, subject to extension if needed.
